- **GitHub App credentials and monitor secrets:** Before first use, release engineering must provision four repository-scoped GitHub Apps plus one separate organization-scoped audit-log monitor App and store their private keys in the narrowest possible GitHub secret scopes: an environment-reader App for `preflight-check` and control-plane monitors, a separate ruleset-auditor App for authoritative Repository Rulesets reads including `bypass_actors`, a release-tag writer App whose private key is stored only in the corresponding `production-tag-write-<project-name>` environment for `create-release-tag`, a release-evidence writer App used only by `require-provenance` to push to `refs/heads/release-evidence`, and a dedicated organization-scoped audit-log monitor App used only by governance monitoring to read organization audit-log events such as emergency-cleanup team membership changes. The environment-reader and ruleset-auditor App private keys required by `official.yml` must be stored only in the matching `control-plane-monitoring-<project-name>` environment for that project. The same credentials, plus the organization-scoped audit-log monitor App private key and any external dead-man's-switch credentials, must be stored in `control-plane-governance-monitoring` for the allowlisted governance workflows. Target-specific publish environments must never carry any audit credential or either write credential. `preflight-check` must mint only the environment-reader and ruleset-auditor tokens; the organization-scoped audit-log monitor App is reserved for the governance and runbook freshness monitor plus any reviewed successor governance workflow. These Apps must request only the permissions required for their single purpose. The required scopes are strict: the environment-reader App must have `actions: read` plus the minimum documented read scope GitHub requires for environment, deployment-policy, and repository Actions settings reads; the ruleset-auditor App must have the minimum GitHub App permission set that returns `bypass_actors` in the Repository Rulesets API, and because GitHub's public docs currently require write access to the ruleset for that field, this design isolates that read-equivalent but permission-elevated credential behind the matching monitoring environment rather than exposing it to every workflow job. Any workflow that mints the ruleset-auditor token must do so only after all trusted and data-only checkouts are complete. While that token is live, the executable boundary is closed: only already-installed reviewed `mise` toolchain binaries and reviewed helpers under `.ctrl-main/eng/scripts/**` may be executed. `.release-src/**` and `.ctrl-main/.github/**` may be inspected only as data and must never be executed, sourced, imported as code, or used as a package-manager root during that window. The allowlisted operation set during that lifetime is therefore exactly: GitHub API reads; read-only inspection of `.release-src/**` and `.ctrl-main/.github/**` data; execution of reviewed normalization/validation helpers under `.ctrl-main/eng/scripts/**`; local `jq`/Python processing driven by those reviewed helpers over already checked-out data; execution of reviewed `mise`-managed toolchain binaries installed before token mint; and token masking/revocation helpers. Installing dependencies, invoking package managers, executing anything from `.release-src/`, or making non-GitHub arbitrary network calls during that window is forbidden. The release-tag writer App must have `contents: write` and no other repository scopes; the release-evidence writer App must have `contents: write` and no other repository scopes. The organization-scoped audit-log monitor App must have only the minimum documented organization-level permission that exposes the organization audit log and no repository mutation scopes. Organization administrators remain the trusted root for these GitHub-hosted secrets; this design does not attempt to defend against org-admin compromise. All private keys and monitor secrets must rotate at least every 90 days and immediately on suspected compromise, and every credential rotation or trusted-publisher selector change must produce a reviewed ledger update that includes `credentialId`, the affected `projectName` and `releaseLine` when project-scoped, the operator rationale, and the verification evidence URL. Any GitHub App installation token minted at runtime must be masked immediately after issuance, before any other use, and should be explicitly revoked at job end on a best-effort basis in addition to relying on its native expiry.
- **Repository administration monitoring:** Changes to production environments, rulesets, bypass actors, GitHub App installations, or other release-control-plane administration state must emit near-real-time alerts. Audit logs remain required, but they are not the only detection mechanism in this design.
- **Alert routing contract:** Every control-plane monitor in this design must declare one of three reviewed routes: `page`, `high-nonpage`, or `tracked-follow-up`. `page` alerts route to the release-engineering primary on-call destination plus a durable team-visible channel, require acknowledgment within 15 minutes, re-page every 30 minutes, and escalate to engineering management at 60 minutes. `high-nonpage` alerts require acknowledgment within 4 hours and must open or update a tracked issue in the same operation. `tracked-follow-up` alerts must open or update a tracked issue by the next business day. Route escalation is superseding rather than duplicative: when one open condition is promoted from `high-nonpage` to `page`, the same tracked incident remains authoritative, the paging route takes precedence for acknowledgment and escalation timing until the incident is downgraded or closed, and monitors must avoid opening a parallel duplicate incident solely to represent the higher route. DMS-provider alerts themselves use the same route as the monitor they protect.
- **Live control-plane drift detection:** In addition to near-real-time administration alerts, the repository must run a dedicated scheduled control-plane drift monitor at least every 30 minutes. This monitor is a named control-plane monitor with its own dual external dead-man's-switch heartbeats and must query every live `control-plane-monitoring-<project-name>` environment, `control-plane-governance-monitoring`, every live target-specific publish environment, every live `buddy-testpypi-<project-name>` environment for projects that declare `pypi:testpypi`, `production-tag-write-<project-name>`, and `production-evidence-write-<project-name>` deployment branch policy, verify that none of those environments has a configured wait timer, verify that no environment in scope contains any deployment tag-policy entry, compare the exact live branch set and publish-environment mapping to `main`'s checked-in `.github/official-caller-refs.json` plus `.github/publish-trust-inventory.json`, verify that `refs/heads/release-evidence` exists and is protected, verify the expected branch and tag ruleset profile including every project-scoped evidence-anchor tag protection, verify the authoritative `bypass_actors` set through the ruleset-auditor App, verify that the required GitHub App installations are present, and verify that the repository Actions settings which control fork-PR approval and pull-request write-token policy remain in the required secure state. For each `control-plane-monitoring-<project-name>` environment, presence and bypass-disabled status are insufficient: its exact deployment branch set must match only that project's authoritative caller-ref subset from `main`. For `control-plane-governance-monitoring`, presence and bypass-disabled status are insufficient: its exact deployment branch set must equal `main` only. For each `buddy-testpypi-<project-name>` environment, presence is also insufficient: it must carry `CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE = publish-pypi-testpypi`, must have no required reviewers and no wait timer, and must have no deployment branch or deployment tag policy configured at all. The monitor must also detect orphan buddy TestPyPI state: any live `buddy-testpypi-<project-name>` environment or any live `pypi:testpypi` trust-inventory entry whose project no longer declares `pypi:testpypi` in `release.json` on `main` is a control-plane incident and must be cleaned up rather than silently ignored. Any mismatch between live GitHub state and `main`'s checked-in caller-ref registry or publish trust inventory is a control-plane incident even if no release is currently running. The drift monitor must route new mismatches as `high-nonpage` immediately, open or update a tracked issue in the same operation, and escalate the same mismatch to `page` only if it persists for more than 4 hours or overlaps any queued, requested, waiting, or in-progress `official.yml` run for the affected project. Registry readiness is isolated from this workflow: `.github/workflows/nuget-trusted-publisher-readiness.yml`, `.github/workflows/npm-trusted-publisher-readiness.yml`, `.github/workflows/pypi-trusted-publisher-readiness.yml`, and `.github/workflows/rubygems-trusted-publisher-readiness.yml` are the canonical writers of their matching snapshot artifacts, each must run with its own reviewed timeout and heartbeat, and failure in one readiness workflow must not suppress fresh snapshot publication for unrelated registries.
- **Official registry auth policy:** `npmjs`, `PyPI`, `RubyGems.org`, and `NuGet.org` all prefer documented GitHub Actions trusted publishing in this design. The authoritative branch restriction for every official target remains the GitHub deployment-branch policy of the corresponding protected environments. Exact provider-side binding to branch, tag, or commit SHA is not assumed for any registry. `NuGet.org` remains one reviewed exception to the "trusted publishing only" runtime path: when upstream `NuGet/login@v1` or its reviewed successor is unavailable or under incident response, `nuget:official` may temporarily switch to the checked-in fallback `authMechanism = api-key-secret` path described above. That fallback remains mutually exclusive with trusted publishing, must be recorded in the trust inventory, and must use the same protected production environment rather than an ad hoc secret source. To keep least privilege explicit, `official.yml` must model those two reviewed NuGet auth modes as two mutually exclusive direct jobs: the trusted-publisher job requests `id-token: write`, while the `api-key-secret` job requests only `contents: read`. `rubygems:official` is the second reviewed exception: it prefers trusted publishing, but may also temporarily switch to the checked-in fallback `authMechanism = api-key-secret` path that uses a scoped push-only RubyGems.org API key carried as `RUBYGEMS_FALLBACK_API_KEY` in the same protected production environment and exposed only as `GEM_HOST_API_KEY` during `gem push`. That fallback remains mutually exclusive with trusted publishing, must be recorded in the trust inventory, and must use the same protected production environment rather than an ad hoc secret source. To keep least privilege symmetric with NuGet, `official.yml` must also model those two reviewed RubyGems auth modes as two mutually exclusive direct jobs: the trusted-publisher job requests `id-token: write`, while the `api-key-secret` job requests only `contents: read`. When `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, the fallback key must be absent; when `authMechanism = api-key-secret`, trusted-publisher selector fields and audience fields must be absent and the job must skip any OIDC request entirely. Repository-side trust inventory is necessary but not sufficient for registry auth readiness, so this design adds reviewed readiness signals before production publication for every production target that depends on trusted-publisher health. `pypi:official` must consume a separate PyPI-family readiness signal produced from a dedicated TestPyPI trusted-publisher canary, and `npm:official` must consume a readiness signal produced from a dedicated public npmjs canary package path. `nuget:official` and `rubygems:official`, by contrast, must consume readiness signals produced from non-mutating trusted-publisher credential exchange checks on the real production providers; the routine monitor stops once the provider accepts the GitHub OIDC identity and returns the expected short-lived publish credential, and it must not push synthetic package versions on a 30-minute cadence. Governance monitoring must execute each reviewed readiness check at least every 30 minutes on GitHub-hosted runners, record the latest reviewed readiness snapshot, and route `high-nonpage` immediately when the check fails, when monitor execution is delayed or missed long enough to violate the 90-minute freshness budget, or when a snapshot write fails. `preflight-check` for any trusted-publisher-backed target must fail closed when the corresponding readiness snapshot is unhealthy, stale, malformed, missing, or classified as a monitor-execution problem. Those fail-closed gates are intentionally broader than provider outages because GitHub publicly documents schedule delay and dropped scheduled runs under load. The recorded readiness `failureClass` must therefore distinguish provider failure from monitor delay or missed schedule so the incident response can fix the right system. If release engineering intentionally wants an end-to-end provider rehearsal for NuGet.org or RubyGems.org beyond that routine credential-exchange signal, it must be a separate manual operation using dedicated canary package identities and monotonically increasing prerelease versions rather than part of the scheduled readiness workflow. When `rubygems:official` uses the reviewed `api-key-secret` fallback, the RubyGems readiness snapshot remains a governance risk signal but does not block that specific production run.
- **Trusted-publisher selector matrix:** GitHub's documented OIDC claims include `workflow_ref` and, for reusable workflows, `job_workflow_ref`; GitHub does not document a stable cross-provider `caller_workflow_ref` abstraction. `npmjs` publicly documents trusted publishing with repository owner, repository name, workflow filename, optional environment, fixed OIDC audience `npm:registry.npmjs.org`, and Node `>= 22.14.0` plus npm CLI `>= 11.5.1` as explicit prerequisites, and its reviewed docs say that when `workflow_call` is used npm validates the calling workflow name rather than the reusable workflow that physically contains `npm publish`. PyPI publicly documents trusted publishing with repository identity and workflow filename, and its troubleshooting docs identify reusable workflows as unsupported because the trusted publisher binds to the workflow identity that appears in the token. PyPI's provider docs do **not** make the same unsupported claim about composite actions: composite actions do not change the workflow identity seen by the provider and therefore are not blocked by the provider-side reusable-workflow limitation. This design still keeps the actual `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` step direct in `official.yml` as a repository policy choice, because the upstream `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` action separately documents composite-action invocation as unsupported for that action's own supported/safe usage model. `RubyGems.org` documents reusable-workflow support, but does not publicly document a required audience value. `NuGet.org` publicly documents GitHub Actions trusted publishing through `NuGet/login@v1` or a reviewed successor that exchanges the OIDC token for a short-lived API key, and the action's public contract also requires an explicit NuGet account username input. This design therefore keeps every official trusted-publisher-backed publish step direct in `official.yml` as a repository policy choice for cross-provider uniformity and audit simplicity, not because every provider would reject reusable-workflow or composite-action indirection in the same way. The repository-side selector for `nuget:official` therefore tracks `nugetUser` in addition to repository, workflow, and environment identity when `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`; when `authMechanism = api-key-secret`, that selector is intentionally absent because no OIDC selector is in force. Exact branch, tag, or commit-SHA binding is not assumed documented in any provider UI and therefore is not part of this design.
- **Trusted-publisher isolation note:** No registry in scope publicly documents stronger isolation between multiple jobs that run inside the same entry workflow and the same protected environment. This design therefore does **not** share one protected environment across official trusted-publisher jobs. Each trusted-publisher-backed target gets its own target-specific environment so the GitHub environment claim, approval queue, and repository-side trust inventory stay target-local.
- **Trusted-publisher and secret change management:** Because external registry auth is coupled to repository identity, trusted-publisher workflow selector path, target-specific production environment name, target auth mechanism, and, where applicable, a fixed documented audience literal or documented runtime discovery behavior in this design, any repository move/rename that changes identity, any change in target auth mechanism, any rename of a target-specific production environment, any rename of `buddy-testpypi-<project-name>`, any change in a fixed documented registry audience, any change in an audience-discovery endpoint, any change in provider-contract status for an incompletely documented provider, any change in the reviewed provider-contract-gap timing fields for such a provider, or any move/rename of a trusted-publisher-backed workflow selector path must be accompanied by the corresponding external configuration update before the next release. Changes to the allowed protected control-plane branch set are GitHub-side operations only in this design: they must update the deployment branch policy on the relevant protected environments, the authoritative checked-in caller-ref registry on `main` at `.github/official-caller-refs.json`, and the matching project entry in `main`'s checked-in publish trust inventory, but they do not require registry-side branch-specific trust edits. The checked-in publish trust inventory must be updated in the same reviewed PR for every trust-bearing target whose trusted selector path, environment, auth mechanism, fixed documented audience literal, audience-discovery endpoint, provider-contract-status field, or provider-contract-gap timing field changed, including `github:official` where no trusted-publisher audience field exists. In this inventory, the trust-bearing target set is every official target plus `pypi:testpypi`; buddy GitHub Packages targets remain excluded because they use only `GITHUB_TOKEN` and do not have external registry-side trusted-publisher state to drift. CI enforces repository-side drift by running the explicit `trusted-release-inventory` job in `ci.yml`, which must compare the post-change trust-bearing state rather than merely checking whether both the inventory file and another control-plane file were edited. The comparison scope is exactly `entryWorkflowPath`, the project-scoped official `allowedCallerRefs` derived from `.github/official-caller-refs.json` as `refs/heads/main` plus only those maintenance refs that match the current project name, and the per-project `language` plus every checked-in trust-bearing target's `publishExecutionPath`, `environment`, `authMechanism`, optional `trustedPublisherSelector`, optional `documentedOidcAudience`, optional `oidcAudienceEndpoint`, optional `providerContractStatus`, optional `providerContractObservedAt`, and optional `providerContractExpiresAt` fields. Order-only differences in `allowedCallerRefs` are not meaningful, but every added, removed, renamed, or remapped caller ref, publish workflow path, environment name, auth mechanism, trusted-publisher selector, fixed audience literal, audience-discovery endpoint, provider-contract-status value, or provider-contract-gap timing value is a hard mismatch. CI must fail any control-plane change for which those post-change values do not exactly match the checked-in inventory, whether or not `.github/publish-trust-inventory.json` itself changed.

**Authoritative official caller-ref registry:** The checked-in authoritative repository-side source of active official caller refs is `.github/official-caller-refs.json` on `refs/heads/main`. This file is not a convenience cache; it is a required control-plane contract that records the normalized fully qualified refs that may dispatch `official.yml`. Official runs from maintenance branches must freeze and consult `main`'s copy rather than any branch-local copy. It uses `schemaVersion: 1` and the exact schema:

```json
{
    "schemaVersion": 1,
    "refs": ["refs/heads/main", "refs/heads/release/example-project/v1.2.x"]
}
```

No top-level keys other than `schemaVersion` and `refs` are allowed. `refs` must be a non-empty array of unique fully qualified Git refs, must contain `refs/heads/main` exactly once, and every non-`main` entry must be an exact fully qualified maintenance branch ref of the form `refs/heads/release/<project-name>/v<major>.<minor>.x`. Tag refs and every other branch shape are invalid in this file. GitHub-side deployment branch policy, the checked-in publish trust inventory, and runtime official caller-ref validation all derive from `main`'s copy of this file rather than from ad hoc branch enumeration or branch-local mirrors.

**Official dispatcher allowlist schema:** The checked-in dispatcher allowlist is also authoritative only on `refs/heads/main` and defines who may start or rerun `official.yml`:

```json
{
    "schemaVersion": 3,
    "users": ["release-engineer-a", "release-engineer-b", "release-flow[bot]"],
    "appIds": ["1234567"],
    "appIdBindings": {
        "1234567": {
            "login": "release-flow[bot]",
            "evidence": "GET /users/release-flow[bot] => id 1234567"
        }
    }
}
```

No top-level keys other than `schemaVersion`, `users`, `appIds`, and `appIdBindings` are allowed. `schemaVersion` must equal `3`. `users` and `appIds` are each optional, but at least one of them must be present and non-empty. `users`, when present, must be an array of unique GitHub login strings, each matching exactly the repository login spelling GitHub reports at runtime; this array may include both human users and GitHub App bot logins when those bot identities are approved to rerun `official.yml`. `appIds`, when present, must be an array of unique decimal-string GitHub **account IDs** for approved GitHub App bot users. Each value must match the bot-user numeric ID that GitHub exposes as `github.actor_id` for an app-triggered run; the GitHub App ID shown on the app settings page is a different identifier and is invalid here. `appIdBindings`, when present, must be an object whose keys are exactly the `appIds` values and whose values each contain exactly `login` and `evidence`. `login` must match one entry in `users` exactly, and `evidence` must be a non-empty same-file reviewed evidence reference or note for that bot-user binding. Any approved GitHub App bot identity is therefore tri-anchored in this file: the bot login appears in `users`, the matching bot-user account ID appears in `appIds`, and the same file records the reviewed binding in `appIdBindings`. A reviewed lookup path is `GET /users/<app-slug>[bot]` and reading the returned `id`. Numeric heuristics alone are not authoritative in this design. Team slugs, role names, wildcard patterns, and mixed untyped actor entries are invalid in this file. `official.yml` must treat this file as the only reviewed actor allowlist for manual official dispatch and rerun admission, while runtime admission still consumes only `users` and `appIds`; `appIdBindings` is machine-readable review evidence and CI validation state rather than a second runtime actor class.

There is no checked-in planned-change-window file in this design. Onboarding, retirement, and emergency cleanup are coordinated operational runbooks that must either reach a converged end state or restore the previous converged state inside one operator session, without leaving durable exception state on `main`. Drift detection still treats any live mismatch between GitHub-side protection and `main`'s checked-in control-plane state as an incident, but onboarding and retirement are handled as bounded high-nonpage control-plane transitions that page only when the mismatch persists beyond the documented budget or overlaps an active official run.

**Publish trust inventory schema:** The checked-in inventory is part of the trusted control plane and is authoritative only on `refs/heads/main`. It uses `schemaVersion: 5` and records one reviewed official control-plane anchor (`entryWorkflowPath: .github/workflows/official.yml`) plus a per-project trust model for every trust-bearing target. In this inventory, the trust-bearing target set is every official target plus buddy `pypi:testpypi`; buddy GitHub Packages targets remain excluded because they publish with `GITHUB_TOKEN` and do not have external registry-side trusted-publisher selectors or OIDC-audience discovery state to drift:

```json
{
    "schemaVersion": 5,
    "entryWorkflowPath": ".github/workflows/official.yml",
    "projects": {
        "example-project": {
            "language": "csharp",
            "currentMainReleaseLine": "1.3.x",
            "allowedCallerRefs": ["refs/heads/main", "refs/heads/release/example-project/v1.2.x"],
            "targets": {
                "nuget:official": {
                    "publishExecutionPath": ".github/workflows/official.yml",
                    "environment": "production-nuget-example-project",
                    "authMechanism": "trusted-publisher",
                    "documentedOidcAudience": "https://www.nuget.org",
                    "trustedPublisherSelector": {
                        "repositoryOwner": "hcoona",
                        "repositoryName": "three",
                        "workflowPath": ".github/workflows/official.yml",
                        "environment": "production-nuget-example-project",
                        "nugetUser": "example-nuget-user"
                    }
                },
                "github:official": {
                    "publishExecutionPath": ".github/workflows/official.yml",
                    "environment": "production-github-example-project",
                    "authMechanism": "github-token"
                }
            }
        }
    }
}
```

The inventory uses fully qualified Git refs under each project's `allowedCallerRefs`, one exact normalized `currentMainReleaseLine`, repository-relative workflow paths, a target-specific environment mapping, an explicit target-to-auth mapping, a target-to-selector mapping for trusted-publisher-backed targets, and either an optional fixed audience literal, an optional audience-discovery endpoint reference, or an optional provider-contract-status marker depending on the provider contract. A project's `allowedCallerRefs` is not an independent source of truth: it must exactly mirror the project-scoped subset derived from `.github/official-caller-refs.json` on `main`, namely `refs/heads/main` plus only those maintenance refs whose path exactly matches `refs/heads/release/<project-name>/v<major>.<minor>.x`. `currentMainReleaseLine` is the authoritative checked-in declaration of which normalized release line `refs/heads/main` is currently allowed to publish for that project, and retired lines must be removed from that field before their retirement is considered complete. When a Python project also declares `pypi:testpypi`, the same `targets` object must include that buddy TestPyPI entry with `publishExecutionPath = .github/workflows/buddy.yml`, `environment = buddy-testpypi-<project-name>`, `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, a `trustedPublisherSelector` bound to the repository owner/name plus workflow path `.github/workflows/buddy.yml` and that same environment name, and `oidcAudienceEndpoint = https://test.pypi.org/_/oidc/audience`. `entryWorkflowPath` remains the reviewed official control-plane anchor for the project-scoped `currentMainReleaseLine` and `allowedCallerRefs` state; buddy TestPyPI does not add a second project-wide caller-ref registry because its steady-state environment policy is intentionally unrestricted by branch.

No top-level keys other than `schemaVersion`, `entryWorkflowPath`, and `projects` are allowed. The validator must enforce this as a strict top-level key whitelist equivalent to JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false`. `projects` must be a non-empty object keyed by exact project name. Every project object must contain exactly `language`, `currentMainReleaseLine`, `allowedCallerRefs`, and `targets`. `language` must use the closed set `{csharp, python, jsts, ruby}`. `currentMainReleaseLine` must be one normalized `<major>.<minor>.x` string. `allowedCallerRefs` must be a non-empty array of unique fully qualified refs. `targets` must be a non-empty object whose keys are drawn only from the trust-bearing target set legal for that project's `language`. In this inventory, the trust-bearing target set is every official target plus `pypi:testpypi`; buddy GitHub Packages targets remain out of scope. Every target object must contain exactly `publishExecutionPath`, `environment`, and `authMechanism`, plus `trustedPublisherSelector` when `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, `documentedOidcAudience` only when the provider publicly documents a fixed audience literal for the selected auth mode, `oidcAudienceEndpoint` only when the provider uses runtime audience discovery and the repository keeps a reviewed endpoint reference for drift/audit purposes, `providerContractStatus` only when the provider still leaves a relevant selector field undocumented in public docs, and `providerContractObservedAt` plus `providerContractExpiresAt` only when `providerContractStatus` is present. The closed `authMechanism` set in this design is `{trusted-publisher, api-key-secret, github-token}`. `api-key-secret` is legal only for `nuget:official` and `rubygems:official`; all other external trust-bearing targets must use `trusted-publisher`, and `github:official` must use `github-token`. Every selector object must contain `repositoryOwner`, `repositoryName`, `workflowPath`, and `environment`. `nuget:official` selectors must also contain `nugetUser`; the other trust-bearing selectors must not add undocumented provider-specific selector keys. When `nuget:official` or `rubygems:official` uses `authMechanism = api-key-secret`, `trustedPublisherSelector`, `documentedOidcAudience`, `oidcAudienceEndpoint`, `providerContractStatus`, `providerContractObservedAt`, and `providerContractExpiresAt` must all be absent because that path intentionally does not rely on OIDC selector matching. Under `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, the fixed-audience set is `{nuget:official, npm:official}`; the audience-discovery-reference set is `{pypi:official, pypi:testpypi}`, where `oidcAudienceEndpoint` is audit/drift state only and must never be passed as a runtime input to `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish`; and `rubygems:official` must currently carry `providerContractStatus = audience-undocumented` because RubyGems public docs still do not publish a required fixed audience value for this design. `providerContractObservedAt` must be an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp that records when release engineering last confirmed that this contract gap still existed from first-party provider documentation, and `providerContractExpiresAt` must be an RFC 3339 UTC timestamp no later than 18 months after `providerContractObservedAt`. Extending that deadline is reviewed contract-gap renewal rather than routine timestamp maintenance: the unresolved-gap renewal count is derived from prior reviewed governance audit records for that same RubyGems contract gap. Renewal count `2` already requires written sign-off from the security committee or organizational security leadership, must add or update one `audit` record with `scope = "control-plane-monitoring-governance"`, and must keep `nextReviewAt` no later than 30 days after merge. Renewal count `3` is the final legal renewal and must also record the concrete transition plan to either adopt the documented audience, switch `rubygems:official` to `authMechanism = api-key-secret`, or fail-close/remove the target; a fourth renewal is invalid. That provider-contract-status marker is audit state only; it does not waive the separate RubyGems readiness-snapshot gate, and the expiry timestamp is a fail-closed deadline rather than a reminder.

The checked-in inventory is an in-repository drift detector and audit trail, not an independent cryptographic proof of registry-side trust state. An actor who can merge arbitrary changes into `main` can change both the workflow code and the inventory together. Its purpose is to make trust changes reviewable and to catch accidental repository-side drift before production approval is consumed.

**Jobs:**

Every job in `official.yml`, including `authorize-dispatcher`, `preflight-check`, `resolve-context`, `static-analysis`, all clean-build jobs, all attestation jobs, `require-provenance`, `create-release-tag`, `confirm-publish-state`, `release-complete`, and all official publish jobs, must run on a GitHub-hosted runner. Self-hosted runners are unsupported for the entire official release pipeline. This is both a repository supply-chain boundary and a reviewed provider-contract alignment: npm trusted publishing currently supports only GitHub-hosted runners, the supported `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` path expects the GitHub-provided Ubuntu VM, and the build artifact itself is part of the later provenance and publication trust boundary.

1. **`authorize-dispatcher`**:
    - Runs before `preflight-check`.
    - `permissions: { contents: read }`
    - This job is intentionally unconditional and must not acquire an `if:` guard.
    - As the first step of `official.yml` and before any git operation, it must assert that `github.ref` starts with `refs/heads/` and hard-fail with a clear non-branch-ref error otherwise. This check runs before `project-name` validation, before resolving `main-control-plane-sha`, and before any checkout of either `main` or the dispatch-selected ref.
    - It must then validate `project-name` with the same syntax rule later used by `resolve-context`, resolve and emit a single immutable `main-control-plane-sha` by reading `refs/heads/main` exactly once, perform a read-only checkout of that exact `main-control-plane-sha` with `persist-credentials: false`, load `.github/official-dispatch-authorizers.json` from that frozen checkout, validate its strict schema, and hard-fail unless the current initial-run actor is allowlisted under the correct actor class: `github.actor` must be present in `users` for a human-triggered run, and `github.actor_id` must be present in `appIds` for an app-triggered run. For app-triggered runs, `appIds` therefore matches the app bot user's GitHub account ID rather than the GitHub App ID.
    - If `github.triggering_actor` is non-empty and differs from `github.actor`, that rerun initiator must also be present in `users`. This rerun check must use `github.triggering_actor`, not `github.actor`. Because GitHub documents `github.actor_id` as the account ID of the initial workflow-run actor, this design does not attempt a parallel rerun numeric-ID check until GitHub documents one.
    - This job must not reference any environment and must not mint any GitHub App token. Its purpose is to ensure that `preflight-check` cannot consume project-scoped monitoring secrets for an unapproved dispatcher.

2. **`preflight-check`**:
    - Runs before `resolve-context`.
    - `needs: [authorize-dispatcher]`
    - `permissions: { contents: read, actions: read }`
    - This job is intentionally unconditional and must not acquire an `if:` guard.
    - This job must run inside `environment: control-plane-monitoring-<project-name>`. Its first in-environment step must validate `CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE = monitoring-preflight` and must self-check that `github.workflow_ref` identifies `.github/workflows/official.yml` at the current ref before it reads any environment secret or mints any GitHub App token. After that self-check succeeds and before any audit token is minted, this job must reuse `needs.authorize-dispatcher.outputs.main-control-plane-sha` as the only authoritative frozen `main` snapshot and must re-emit that exact value unchanged as `preflight-check.outputs.main-control-plane-sha` for downstream jobs. Every later read of checked-in control-plane files and every helper executed while project-scoped monitoring credentials remain live must be pinned to that exact SHA; `preflight-check` must not re-read moving `main` state later in the run. That frozen SHA is an approval-time revocation boundary, not a lifetime waiver: if later monitoring finds that current `refs/heads/main` no longer matches the frozen SHA and the intervening diff touches `.github/official-caller-refs.json`, `.github/official-dispatch-authorizers.json`, `.github/publish-trust-inventory.json`, `.github/provenance-signer-map.json`, `.github/release-recovery-ledger.jsonl`, or any `.github/release-recovery-ledger-archive-*.jsonl` file, the run becomes control-plane-revoked and must lose approval eligibility under the monitor rules defined in Section 7.
    - Before its first privileged GitHub API read and before any audit token is minted, this job must perform two read-only checkouts in distinct directories: a frozen checkout of `main` at `needs.authorize-dispatcher.outputs.main-control-plane-sha` under `path: .ctrl-main` for trusted control-plane helpers and control-plane files, plus a separate checkout of the dispatch-selected protected source ref under `path: .release-src` for data-only inspection. It must validate `project-name` with the same syntax rule as `resolve-context`, re-assert the already-checked `refs/heads/` caller-ref invariant as a defensive guard, resolve `project-path` and `language`, read the project's `release.json`, apply the same language-target validation used later by `resolve-context`, filter to the official target set, fail if that filtered set is empty, and derive the exact required environment names for that project: `control-plane-monitoring-<project-name>`, one target-specific publish environment per selected official target, plus `production-tag-write-<project-name>` and `production-evidence-write-<project-name>`. Only after that local compatibility and target-set validation succeeds may it mint the two dedicated GitHub App installation tokens just in time: an environment-reader token for GitHub Environments and deployment branch policy reads, and a separate ruleset-auditor token for authoritative Repository Rulesets reads including `bypass_actors`. A long-lived PAT is not the normal path. The GitHub App private keys for these audit tokens must live only in the matching `control-plane-monitoring-<project-name>` environment, not in organization-level or repository-level general workflow secrets. Treat the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` as insufficient for this job; weakening or skipping the verification is unsupported. Every minted installation token must be masked before first use.
    - Any helper code used before the job leaves the monitoring environment must come only from `.ctrl-main/`; `.release-src/` remains data-only during the ruleset-auditor token lifetime. While the ruleset-auditor token is live, the executable boundary is exact: only already-installed reviewed `mise` toolchain binaries and reviewed helpers under `.ctrl-main/eng/scripts/**` may be executed. `.release-src/**` and `.ctrl-main/.github/**` are data sources only and must never be executed, sourced, imported as code, or used as package-manager roots during that window. The allowed operation set is therefore closed to GitHub API reads; read-only inspection of `.release-src/**` and frozen `.ctrl-main/.github/**` data; execution of reviewed normalization/validation helpers under `.ctrl-main/eng/scripts/**`; local `jq`/Python processing driven by those reviewed helpers over already checked-out data; execution of reviewed `mise`-managed toolchain binaries installed before token mint; and token masking/revocation helpers. Executing any `.release-src/` code, installing dependencies, invoking package managers, or making non-GitHub arbitrary network calls during that window is forbidden.
    - Before any production approval is consumed, this job must also enumerate live runs of `.github/workflows/official.yml` in `queued`, `requested`, `waiting`, or `in_progress` state and hard-fail if another run for the same validated `project-name` already exists on a different ref. The current run ID is excluded from this check. This is an advisory same-project cross-ref admission lock rather than a transactional security boundary, because GitHub does not document an atomic repository-wide workflow-run reservation primitive. If this check fails because another run is already live, the losing run must stop before any approval is granted. If two runs nevertheless overlap because they raced between enumeration and later state transition, `.github/workflows/official-run-health-monitor.yml` must treat that overlap as a `high-nonpage` incident, identify the losing run with the same later-created-or-not-yet-environment-gated rule defined above, and auto-cancel that losing run within 15 minutes whenever it has not yet reached `create-release-tag`, `require-provenance`, or any selected publish job. If both runs have already reached environment-gated jobs or later mutation stages, the monitor must escalate to `page` immediately and route operators into the partial-run recovery path rather than leaving both approvals live.
    - Before any production approval is consumed, this job must also enumerate completed `official.yml` runs for the same validated `project-name` in descending `created_at` order with `per_page=100` and a reviewed page-budget constant. That scan is project-history based rather than limited to the current protected control-plane branch set, because a later caller-ref retirement must not hide an older unresolved same-project blocker. The stop condition is intentionally strict: continue until GitHub reports no more completed same-project runs. Exhausting the configured page budget before proving that the completed same-project history was exhausted is a hard fail-closed `same-project-completed-run-scan-incomplete` result; this job must not guess that older unseen runs are irrelevant just because a newer run already settled cleanly. For every scanned completed run, parse any immutable `candidate-ledger-payload-<project-name>-<run-id>-attempt-<run-attempt>` artifact it published. When such a payload declares `admissionBlock = true`, carries one exact `auditId` or `incidentId`, and the frozen main ledger does not yet contain that same record ID at any revision, this run must hard-fail immediately even if no reviewed ledger PR has been opened or merged yet. This makes the candidate payload itself a temporary fail-closed admission fact for blocking anomalies such as `confirmation-alert = serial-degraded`; once the corresponding record reaches `main`, the ordinary ledger checks below become authoritative. Payloads with `admissionBlock = false`, such as the `single-release-identity` audit emitted for `npm-native-provenance-classification = intentionally-disabled`, remain durable audit inputs but do not themselves block same-project admission. The same completed-run scan must also inspect the immutable `tag-reservation-result-<project-name>` artifact and the completed run conclusion for any other scanned same-project official run that already reached `create-release-tag`. If another completed run successfully reserved or reused the official tag for a release identity but did not later finish `release-complete` successfully, this run must hard-fail unless the frozen main ledger already contains a later reviewed terminal record that explicitly closes, abandons, burns, withdraws, or otherwise settles that exact release identity. A completed post-tag official run with no successful terminal reconciliation is therefore itself a temporary same-project admission blocker rather than a state that later dispatches may ignore while waiting for asynchronous bookkeeping.
    - Before any production approval is consumed, this job must also load the frozen `.github/release-recovery-ledger.jsonl` from `needs.authorize-dispatcher.outputs.main-control-plane-sha`, evaluate only the latest revision of each incident and audit with the reviewed ledger helper from `.ctrl-main/eng/scripts/**`, and hard-fail if either (a) the same `project-name` has any still-open incident whose `indeterminateTargets` array is non-empty or whose `disposition` is `open-before-publish` or `open-partial-publish`, or (b) the same `project-name` has any still-open `audit` record with `scope = "control-plane-monitoring-project"`, `result = "discrepancy-found"`, and `followUpStatus = "required-open"`. This is a mechanical dispatch block, not an operator checklist. The failure output must print at least the blocking `incidentId` or `auditId`, the relevant incident disposition or `indeterminateTargets`, the audit scope when applicable, and `nextReviewAt` so operators know which unresolved control-plane or release-state issue must be cleared before a new official attempt may proceed.
    - Verifies that every derived required environment already exists; that every target-specific publish environment plus the tag-write and evidence-write environments includes a required-reviewer protection rule with at least two reviewers total, `prevent_self_review` enabled, administrator bypass disabled, no configured wait timer, and the exact deployment branch set from `main`'s caller-ref registry for that project; and that the publish, tag-write, and evidence-write environments expose the same reviewer pool and the same branch-policy set. `control-plane-monitoring-<project-name>` is validated separately and must have no required-reviewer rule, no wait timer, and deployment branches exactly equal only the selected project's protected control-plane branch set frozen from `.github/official-caller-refs.json`. Any mismatch in that project-scoped set blocks only official runs for that same project and is therefore the mechanism that enforces the project-local hold during onboarding or retirement transitions.
    - Uses the GitHub Environments API response directly: the check must look for a `protection_rules` entry with `type == "required_reviewers"` and a reviewer list whose total length is at least `2`, must verify `prevent_self_review == true`, must verify that administrator bypass is disabled, must verify that no `wait_timer` protection rule is present, and must verify that the deployment branch policy on the publish, tag-write, and evidence-write environments contains exactly the expected branch names for `main` plus the registered protected maintenance branches for that project, with no missing entry and no extra entry. The same API pass must verify that `control-plane-monitoring-<project-name>` contains exactly that selected project's protected control-plane branch set frozen from `main`, with no missing entry and no extra entry. Wildcard or pattern-based entries such as `release/**`, and every deployment tag-policy entry, are hard failures. Because the API returns short branch names rather than fully qualified refs, this job must normalize the expected caller refs by stripping the `refs/heads/` prefix before comparison. Required reviewers and exact branch policy are both mandatory; a wait timer or branch policy alone is not sufficient. This job must fail closed on any live environment branch-set mismatch before later production approvals are consumed, while `resolve-context` separately verifies that the checked-in publish trust inventory and checked-in caller-ref registry agree with each other. `refs/heads/release-evidence` is outside that environment-derived branch set by design.
    - Uses the GitHub Repository Rulesets API only. It must verify that active branch rulesets protect `main`, every non-`main` branch currently allowed by the relevant target-specific publish, tag-write, evidence-write, or `control-plane-monitoring-<project-name>` deployment policies for that project, and the exact branch `refs/heads/release-evidence` with the required profile for each ref. The protected release branches must carry the same required PR review, required code-owner review, required status check `ci-passed`, no direct pushes, and no force-pushes, and their bypass actors must be limited to the dedicated release-engineering emergency-cleanup group rather than broad repository roles or the GitHub Actions app. `refs/heads/release-evidence` must be protected against direct pushes, force-push, and deletion and must allow bypass only for the dedicated release-evidence writer App plus the dedicated release-engineering emergency-cleanup group. The job must also verify that an active tag ruleset protects `refs/tags/release/**` against unauthorized creation and updates, that a second active tag ruleset or prefix-targeted ruleset protects `refs/tags/control-plane/release-evidence-head/<project-name>`, and that their bypass actors are limited to the dedicated release-tag writer App for `refs/tags/release/**` plus the dedicated release-evidence writer App for the selected project's evidence-anchor tag, with the dedicated release-engineering emergency-cleanup group as the only human bypass actor for both.
    - Before any production approval is consumed, this job must also read the JIT reconciliation snapshot through the exact artifact contract defined above: latest successful `.github/workflows/official-run-health-monitor.yml` run on `refs/heads/main`, exact artifact `jit-reconciliation-snapshot`, exact file `jit-reconciliation-snapshot.json`, strict `schemaVersion: 1` parsing, `result == healthy`, and `newestSuccessfulReconciliationAt` newer than 30 minutes. Missing run metadata, missing artifact, malformed JSON, missing required keys, `result in {failed, unknown}`, or a stale timestamp are all the same fail-closed `jit-membership-stale` condition. Governance alerting remains required, but alerting alone is not sufficient: this is the technical admission gate that blocks official release while `jit-membership-stale` is in effect. The same design also forbids using GitHub's platform-scale approval window as an operational holding area: any `official.yml` run that remains `requested` or `waiting` on a protected evidence, tag-write, or publish environment for more than 8 hours must be auto-cancelled by `.github/workflows/official-run-health-monitor.yml` and resumed only through a fresh dispatch so JIT and control-plane health are re-evaluated from scratch.
        - When the resolved official target set includes `nuget:official` and the frozen inventory entry selects `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, this job must also read the NuGet trusted-publisher readiness snapshot through the exact artifact contract defined above: latest successful `.github/workflows/nuget-trusted-publisher-readiness.yml` run on `refs/heads/main`, exact artifact `nuget-trusted-publisher-readiness-snapshot`, exact file `nuget-trusted-publisher-readiness-snapshot.json`, strict `schemaVersion: 1` parsing, `status == healthy`, `failureClass == none`, `checkMode == credential-exchange`, `sourceSha == needs.authorize-dispatcher.outputs.main-control-plane-sha`, and `observedAt` newer than 90 minutes. Missing run metadata, missing artifact, malformed JSON, missing required keys, `status in {failed, unknown}`, `failureClass != none`, `checkMode != credential-exchange`, a mismatched `sourceSha`, or a stale timestamp are all fail-closed readiness states. The reviewed readiness source is the non-mutating OIDC-to-temporary-key exchange itself; this design intentionally does not require a scheduled NuGet production package publish canary.
        - When the resolved official target set includes `npm:official`, this job must also read the npm trusted-publisher readiness snapshot through the exact artifact contract defined above: latest successful `.github/workflows/npm-trusted-publisher-readiness.yml` run on `refs/heads/main`, exact artifact `npm-trusted-publisher-readiness-snapshot`, exact file `npm-trusted-publisher-readiness-snapshot.json`, strict `schemaVersion: 1` parsing, `status == healthy`, `failureClass == none`, `sourceSha == needs.authorize-dispatcher.outputs.main-control-plane-sha`, and `observedAt` newer than 90 minutes. Missing run metadata, missing artifact, malformed JSON, missing required keys, `status in {failed, unknown}`, `failureClass != none`, a mismatched `sourceSha`, or a stale timestamp are all fail-closed readiness states.
        - When the resolved official target set includes `pypi:official`, this job must also read the PyPI trusted-publisher readiness snapshot through the exact artifact contract defined above: latest successful `.github/workflows/pypi-trusted-publisher-readiness.yml` run on `refs/heads/main`, exact artifact `pypi-trusted-publisher-readiness-snapshot`, exact file `pypi-trusted-publisher-readiness-snapshot.json`, strict `schemaVersion: 1` parsing, `status == healthy`, `failureClass == none`, `canaryTarget == testpypi`, `sourceSha == needs.authorize-dispatcher.outputs.main-control-plane-sha`, and `observedAt` newer than 90 minutes. Missing run metadata, missing artifact, malformed JSON, missing required keys, `status in {failed, unknown}`, `failureClass != none`, a wrong `canaryTarget`, a mismatched `sourceSha`, or a stale timestamp are all fail-closed readiness states.
        - When the resolved official target set includes `rubygems:official` and the frozen inventory entry selects `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, this job must also read the RubyGems trusted-publisher readiness snapshot through the exact artifact contract defined above: latest successful `.github/workflows/rubygems-trusted-publisher-readiness.yml` run on `refs/heads/main`, exact artifact `rubygems-trusted-publisher-readiness-snapshot`, exact file `rubygems-trusted-publisher-readiness-snapshot.json`, strict `schemaVersion: 1` parsing, `status == healthy`, `failureClass == none`, `checkMode == credential-exchange`, `sourceSha == needs.authorize-dispatcher.outputs.main-control-plane-sha`, and `observedAt` newer than 90 minutes. Missing run metadata, missing artifact, malformed JSON, missing required keys, `status in {failed, unknown}`, `failureClass != none`, `checkMode != credential-exchange`, a mismatched `sourceSha`, or a stale timestamp are all fail-closed readiness states. The reviewed readiness source is the non-mutating OIDC-to-short-lived-credential exchange itself; this design intentionally does not require a scheduled RubyGems production gem publish canary. When the same frozen inventory entry instead selects `authMechanism = api-key-secret`, the latest RubyGems readiness snapshot remains a required governance signal but does not block that specific run.
    - Before any approval is consumed, this job must also verify through the refs API that `refs/heads/release-evidence` and `refs/tags/control-plane/release-evidence-head/<project-name>` already exist for the selected project. It must also dereference both refs, verify that the project-scoped anchor tag resolves to a commit object, and prove that that commit is reachable from the current `refs/heads/release-evidence` tip for the same repository state. A dangling anchor, a non-commit target, or an anchor that points outside the current `release-evidence` branch lineage is a hard failure. Ruleset presence alone is insufficient because rulesets do not create or validate those refs.
    - `preflight-check` must not claim to machine-enforce the emergency-cleanup group's maximum size or reviewer-overlap policy; those are governance checks performed out of band because neither the environment-reader App nor the ruleset-auditor App enumerates team membership.
    - Treats every GitHub API error as a hard failure. Specifically: `404` from environment endpoints means one or more required target-specific publish environments or the tag/evidence-write environments are missing; a successful API response that lacks the required reviewers rule where one is required, has `prevent_self_review` disabled, has a wildcard deployment branch policy, lacks the required branch or tag rulesets, or applies a weaker ruleset profile than `main` means the protected environment set is misconfigured; every other non-`200` response blocks the workflow as an environment-verification failure.
    - Fails hard if the environment is missing or unprotected. This turns the documented prerequisite into an executable guardrail.
    - All GitHub API calls in this job must set an explicit client timeout of no more than 30 seconds per request so the guard fails fast rather than consuming the full job timeout on a hung response.
    - This check is still an audit-before-use guard, not a transactional lock. If an administrator weakens or deletes environment protection after `preflight-check` passes but before a later job reaches its environment gate, the authoritative fail-closed path is the later GitHub environment evaluation plus that job's required `CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE` check; a deleted environment must therefore stop the run by appearing as an uninitialized auto-created environment rather than by silently proceeding. The same residual TOCTOU window exists for tag rulesets: `preflight-check` validates the live ruleset configuration at job start, while `create-release-tag` is still subject to whatever tag ruleset is live at push time. Those residual windows are accepted and must be controlled through CODEOWNERS, repository audit logs, and change discipline around production protection settings.

3. **`resolve-context`**:
    - `needs: [preflight-check]`
    - `permissions: { contents: read }`
    - **Input validation (first step, before checkout):** Validate `project-name` with a full-string match against `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*`, require length `1..100`, reject any occurrence of `..`, reject trailing `.`, and reject any name that ends with `.lock`. Reject invalid names with a clear error. Releasable project identities in this design are ASCII-lowercase only.
    - **Runner and tooling:** Runs on `ubuntu-latest`. Like `resolve-context` in `buddy.yml`, version resolution uses the repository-local `nbgv-python` adapter from the checked-out source ref and does not require a Windows runner even for C# projects. The job must hard-fail if `mise.lock` is absent, and should restore a tool cache keyed by `mise.toml` and `mise.lock` before invoking `mise install`. If the lockfile needs regeneration, that is an out-of-band repository change performed with `mise lock`, not a workflow fallback. Every tool used in an official build or publish path must use a digest-pinning backend; version-string-only backends are unsupported in this design. Before this official-path job invokes `mise install`, it must satisfy the Section 1 bootstrap trust-root rule by either verifying the `mise` executable against reviewed integrity data or operating under the explicitly reviewed GitHub-hosted runner-image trust-root assumption. If `nbgv-python` cannot resolve the version deterministically, the job must hard-fail; there is no fallback or manual override path in this design.
    - **Source checkout:** Check out the dispatch-selected protected source ref for this workflow run with `fetch-depth: 0` and `persist-credentials: false`. In `official.yml`, that source workspace is both the trusted control-plane checkout and the release payload input.
    - Runs `eng/scripts/find_project_path.py` to resolve `language` and `project-path` from `project-name`. `project-name` is ASCII-lowercase and must resolve to exactly one releasable project in the repository whose leaf directory name uses that same canonical lowercase spelling. The resolution step must emit exactly one of `{csharp, python, jsts, ruby}` for `language`; no match, ambiguous match, unsupported language, or resolver error is a hard failure.
    - **NBGV resolution and semantic validation:** Resolve the version with `nbgv-python`, hard-fail if that resolution is non-deterministic, and use the resolved value as the workflow output `version`. Here, "non-deterministic" has the same meaning as in `buddy.yml`: no unique governing `version.json`, no unique normalized version string from the selected full-history checkout, or validator rejection of the resolved string. Inheriting the nearest ancestor `version.json` when the project root does not have its own local file is intentional, but the governing file must still resolve uniquely. Then validate that resolved version using `eng/scripts/validate_semver2_version.py` (NuGet and npm), `eng/scripts/validate_rubygems_version.py` (the repository's supported RubyGems-compatible subset), or `eng/scripts/validate_pep440_version.py --channel official` (Python), chosen after the project language is known. The Python validator must receive that explicit channel flag; default-mode inference is unsupported. `eng/scripts/validate_pep440_version.py --channel official` must reject non-canonical normalized PEP 440 strings, all epoch markers (`!`), all local version identifiers (`+...`), and all `.devN` development-release forms on the official release path. `.postN` post-releases remain valid on the official release path and derive the same `<release-line>` as their base release. `eng/scripts/validate_semver2_version.py` must reject official release versions that contain SemVer build metadata (`+...`).
    - **Official branch-line validation:** Derive `<release-line>` using the release-line derivation rule above. This job must reuse `needs.preflight-check.outputs.main-control-plane-sha` as its only authoritative `main` snapshot and must not recapture or recompute against moving `origin/main` state. It must require the current caller ref to start with `refs/heads/`, then read `.github/official-caller-refs.json` from that frozen snapshot and require the current caller ref to be listed there. If the current caller ref is `refs/heads/main`, the branch-shape check succeeds only provisionally at this stage: `refs/heads/main` must be present in the frozen caller-ref registry, and the later publish trust inventory preflight must additionally prove that the matching project inventory entry exists, still includes `refs/heads/main`, and declares `currentMainReleaseLine` exactly equal to the derived `<release-line>`. If the current caller ref is not `refs/heads/main`, it must be exactly `refs/heads/release/<project-name>/v<release-line>`, and that exact ref must be present in both the frozen caller-ref registry and the derived project-scoped `allowedCallerRefs` entry. The workflow does not infer branch eligibility by comparing against `main`'s current release line; it uses the checked-in caller-ref registry plus the checked-in per-project `currentMainReleaseLine` field.
    - Reads `release.json` from the selected source workspace, validates it exactly as specified in **Section 5**, applies the same language-target validation rule as `buddy.yml`, then filters to the official target set `{nuget:official, npm:official, pypi:official, rubygems:official, github:official}` and fails if the filtered set is empty.
    - **Official npm dist-tag derivation:** If `npm:official` is present in the filtered target set, derive `npm-dist-tags` deterministically as a compact ordered JSON array from the validated caller ref, release line, and whether the resolved version is stable or prerelease. Stable releases from `refs/heads/main` use `["latest"]`. Stable releases from a maintenance branch `refs/heads/release/<project-name>/v<release-line>` use `["release-v<major>.<minor>"]` and must never append `latest`. Prerelease versions remain eligible for official publication, but they must never claim `latest`: lowercase the first prerelease identifier and use that entire identifier as the prerelease channel token. That token is subject to two independent rules. First, it must not begin with `v`, because a leading `v` conflicts semantically with version-prefix conventions and is forbidden regardless of how the structural regex evolves in the future. Second, it must match `^[a-uw-z][a-z0-9]*$`; numeric-leading identifiers, numeric-only identifiers, identifiers containing separators such as `-`, `.`, or `_`, and identifiers beginning with `v` are unsupported for `npm:official` and must hard-fail in `resolve-context`. The derived prerelease channel token must then be validated structurally and contextually before any maintenance-line prefix is added: it must not equal `latest`, must not equal `buddy`, must not equal `release`, must not begin with `release-v`, and must not begin with `rv`. The `rv*` prefix family is reserved in this design to avoid ambiguity with maintenance-line `release-v*` tags. Prerelease releases from `main` therefore use tags such as `rc`, `beta`, `alpha`, `preview`, or `next`; prerelease releases from maintenance branches use `["release-v<major>.<minor>-<channel>"]`. These four cases are the complete deterministic tag families for official npm publication: `{latest}`, `{<channel>}`, `{release-v<major>.<minor>}`, `{release-v<major>.<minor>-<channel>}`. Tags may move forward only within their own family; there is no cross-family retargeting between `latest`, prerelease-channel tags, maintenance-line stable tags, and maintenance-line prerelease tags. `resolve-context` must perform this structural validation before emitting `npm-dist-tags`, and the direct `publish-npm-official` job in `official.yml` must validate the emitted tag array against runtime `github.ref` and `release-line` before any registry mutation.
    - **Official npm native-provenance intent:** If `npm:official` is present in the filtered target set, `resolve-context` must also validate `github.event.inputs.npm-native-provenance-intent` against the closed set `{auto, disabled}`, default it to `auto` when omitted, and emit it unchanged as `npm-native-provenance-intent`. `disabled` is a reviewed operator override that makes `intentionally-disabled` a legal classification path for otherwise eligible npm-native provenance runs. Objective ineligibility still wins: a private repository or restricted package must classify to the corresponding `not-applicable-*` state even when the operator requested `disabled`. That override is not audit-free: if the later same-run classification settles as `intentionally-disabled`, the successful official attempt must trigger the reviewed recovery-ledger update path so one `audit` record is created for the same release identity with `scope = "single-release-identity"`, `result = "discrepancy-found"`, `evidenceUrl` pointing to the workflow run URL, and `nextReviewAt` no later than 7 days after the run. If `npm:official` is absent, `resolve-context` must hard-fail on any explicit non-default value rather than silently accepting an unreachable provenance override; the workflow-dispatch description is intentionally npm-only so operators see that constraint before the run starts.
    - **Official npm toolchain floor:** If `npm:official` is present in the filtered target set, `resolve-context` must also read the reviewed locked toolchain state from the selected source ref and hard-fail unless the production path pins Node `>= 22.14.0` and npm CLI `>= 11.5.1`. `trusted-release-inventory` and `hk check --all` must enforce the same invariant on candidate control-plane changes so this normally fails before production dispatch.
    - **Repository visibility fact:** If `npm:official` is present in the filtered target set, `resolve-context` must also derive and emit `repository-visibility` as exactly one of `{public, private}` from the current run's GitHub repository metadata. This emitted value is the authoritative same-run repository-visibility fact for npm-native-provenance classification and later confirmation. That same-run fact is a deliberate design choice rather than a claim that repository visibility cannot drift later; if repository visibility changes after `resolve-context`, that late drift is an operational anomaly to investigate, not a reason for later steps to silently reclassify the already-frozen release attempt from new live reads. If `npm:official` is absent, `resolve-context` may omit that output.
    - **Publish trust inventory preflight:** After the official target set is resolved, read `.github/official-caller-refs.json` and `.github/publish-trust-inventory.json` from the same frozen `main` control-plane snapshot, validate both schemas, verify that `entryWorkflowPath` is exactly `.github/workflows/official.yml`, verify that the current caller ref is present in `.github/official-caller-refs.json`, look up the exact `projects[<project-name>]` entry, verify that its `language` equals the resolved project language, verify that its `currentMainReleaseLine` is present and exactly equals the normalized derived `<release-line>` whenever the current caller ref is `refs/heads/main`, derive the expected project-scoped `allowedCallerRefs` as `refs/heads/main` plus only those maintenance refs in `.github/official-caller-refs.json` that exactly match `refs/heads/release/<project-name>/v<major>.<minor>.x`, verify that the inventory entry matches that derived subset exactly, verify that every filtered official target declared by the validated `release.json` has an exact matching per-target object in the inventory, and verify that any extra inventory target outside that filtered official set is allowed only when it is another declared trust-bearing non-official target for the same project, currently `pypi:testpypi`. It must then verify that every filtered official target maps to an exact per-target object that defines the expected publish execution path, target-specific environment name, auth mode, optional trusted-publisher selector contract, and, when applicable, an optional fixed OIDC audience literal, optional audience-discovery endpoint reference, or optional provider-contract-status marker plus its required timing fields. Official auth modes are `trusted-publisher` for `npm:official` and `pypi:official`; `nuget:official` and `rubygems:official` may use either `trusted-publisher` or the reviewed fallback `api-key-secret`; and `github:official` uses `github-token`. When `npm:official` is selected, `resolve-context` must also copy that target's inventory `documentedOidcAudience` value into `npm-oidc-audience` and currently require it to equal `npm:registry.npmjs.org`; `publish-npm-official` must reject any runtime mismatch against that emitted value before registry mutation. For `pypi:official`, `oidcAudienceEndpoint` is repository audit/drift state only: `resolve-context` must validate the reviewed endpoint reference but must not emit it as a runtime publish input, because `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` performs audience discovery internally. For `rubygems:official`, when `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, `providerContractStatus` must currently equal `audience-undocumented`, `documentedOidcAudience` must remain absent until RubyGems publishes a stable audience contract, and both `providerContractObservedAt` plus `providerContractExpiresAt` must be present and well formed. While that status remains `audience-undocumented`, the repository must treat it as a bounded temporary contract gap rather than a permanent steady state: the governance monitor must keep probing for a published RubyGems audience contract, any newly documented fixed audience must be triaged as a `high-nonpage` control-plane change within 24 hours, the separate RubyGems readiness snapshot gate must still remain healthy before each run, the checked-in inventory plus runtime validation must be updated or the target must be fail-closed within 30 days of first confirmed provider documentation, and `resolve-context` must hard-fail once the current time is later than `providerContractExpiresAt` even if the provider still has not published a fixed audience contract. Extending that deadline is not an operational no-op: it requires a reviewed control-plane PR that refreshes `providerContractObservedAt`, records new first-party evidence for the still-missing contract, and keeps the new expiry within 18 months of the refreshed observation. The unresolved-gap renewal count is derived from the reviewed governance-audit trail for that same RubyGems contract gap. Renewal count `2` already requires written sign-off from the security committee or organizational security leadership as a merge prerequisite, must add or update one `audit` record with `scope = "control-plane-monitoring-governance"`, and must keep `nextReviewAt` no later than 30 days after merge. Renewal count `3` is the final legal renewal, must also record the concrete transition plan to either adopt the documented audience, switch `rubygems:official` to `authMechanism = api-key-secret`, or fail-close/remove the target, and the daily governance-and-runbook-freshness monitor must escalate that same unresolved gap to `page`. A fourth renewal is invalid and `resolve-context` must fail closed if the frozen inventory would require it. When `rubygems:official` instead selects `authMechanism = api-key-secret`, `trustedPublisherSelector`, `documentedOidcAudience`, `oidcAudienceEndpoint`, `providerContractStatus`, `providerContractObservedAt`, and `providerContractExpiresAt` must all be absent, and `resolve-context` must emit `rubygems-auth-mechanism` directly from the frozen inventory entry for the later direct publish job. When `nuget:official` is selected, `resolve-context` must also emit `nuget-auth-mechanism` directly from the frozen inventory entry, and the later selected `publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher` or `publish-nuget-official-api-key` job must pass that exact frozen value into `.github/actions/publish-nuget-official` without reinterpretation. For `nuget:official`, any documented audience value remains audit and drift state only when `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, because the runtime OIDC exchange is delegated to `NuGet/login@v1` or its reviewed successor rather than to a caller-supplied audience input; the fallback `api-key-secret` path must instead prove that all OIDC selector fields are absent. This catches repository-side trust drift before any production approval is consumed. Because registry-side trust settings are not queried portably, matching external configuration updates are still a mandatory operational step.
    - **Official release tag derivation and overwrite guard:** Derive `tag-name = release/<project-name>/v<version>`. This guard must query the remote protected tag namespace via `git ls-remote --tags` or the GitHub refs API rather than relying on a local tag list from checkout. When `git ls-remote --tags` is used, annotated tags must be compared by their peeled `refs/tags/<tag>^{}` commit SHA rather than by the raw tag-object SHA at `refs/tags/<tag>`. If that protected official release tag already exists and points to a different commit, fail immediately. If it already exists and points to the current commit, treat the tag reservation as an idempotent no-op. If `github:official` is among the resolved targets, check GitHub Releases state for that derived tag. If no GitHub Release exists for that derived tag, proceed — this is the normal first official run. Official GitHub Releases must use a deterministic release title `<project-name> v<version>`. The conflict scan uses two reviewed passes. First, it must enumerate the protected tag namespace with the exact prefix `release/<project-name>/v` through the refs API, `git ls-remote`, or an equivalent reviewed exact-prefix mechanism, then inspect GitHub Release records whose tag name belongs to that project-scoped namespace. Second, it must perform an exact-title equality scan for `<project-name> v<version>` across repository GitHub Releases so namespace-external manual or legacy releases cannot be ignored. Pagination is required for both passes, using `per_page=100` and reviewed configurable page-budget constants. If either scan exhausts its budget before proving completion, it must fail closed with `release-title-scan-cap-exceeded`, must require a tracked audit using the reviewed helper `eng/scripts/official_release_title_scan.py`, and must not silently treat the truncated result as exhaustive. That helper is the canonical operator tool for this incident class: it must reuse the same deterministic-title and stable-identity rules as the workflow, restart both reviewed passes from page 1 against the live API snapshot at helper execution time rather than resuming from the workflow's truncated page offset, deduplicate by immutable `releaseId`, and emit a machine-readable JSON report with exactly the top-level keys `schemaVersion`, `scanStartedAt`, `scanCompletedAt`, `currentReleaseIdentity`, and `scanPasses`. `currentReleaseIdentity` must be the comparison anchor for the failed run and must include exactly `tagName`, `version`, and `sourceCommit`. `scanPasses` is exact rather than illustrative: it must contain exactly two objects. The `project-tag-namespace` pass object must contain exactly `passName`, `filterKind`, `filterValue`, `tagEnumeration`, `releaseEnumeration`, and `results`, where `filterKind = tag-prefix`, `filterValue = release/<project-name>/v`, `tagEnumeration` contains exactly `source`, `pageRangeExamined`, and `exhausted`, `source` is fixed to `refs-api`, `tagEnumeration.pageRangeExamined` contains exactly `startPage`, `endPage`, and `perPage`, and `releaseEnumeration` contains exactly `pageRangeExamined` and `exhausted` with the same `pageRangeExamined` shape. The `exact-title-equality` pass object must contain exactly `passName`, `filterKind`, `filterValue`, `releaseEnumeration`, and `results`, where `filterKind = exact-title`, `filterValue = <project-name> v<version>`, and `releaseEnumeration` again contains exactly `pageRangeExamined` and `exhausted`. Every helper-side `pageRangeExamined.startPage` must equal `1` because the helper proves exhaustion only through a fresh full rescan. Each `results[]` item must contain exactly `releaseId`, `matchedByPass`, `createdAt`, `title`, `tagName`, `tagLookupState`, `peeledTagTargetCommitSha`, `releaseTargetCommitishValue`, `isPrerelease`, and `isDraft`. `matchedByPass` must equal the parent `passName`; `tagLookupState` must be one of `{resolved, missing}`; `peeledTagTargetCommitSha` is the peeled commit SHA for `tagName` when `tagLookupState = resolved` and must be absent when `tagLookupState = missing`; and `releaseTargetCommitishValue` is the exact GitHub Release API `target_commitish` string rather than a resolver-derived commit SHA. The helper report is evidence, not standalone clearance: if it finds no conflict, operators still need a reviewed control-plane change that removes the bounded-scan failure before a fresh official dispatch is allowed. An interrupted, truncated, or otherwise incomplete scan is `unknown`, not `not found`, and the helper's enumeration metadata is evidence of a fresh snapshot-time rescan rather than of continuation from the original failed workflow page budget.
