Match that deterministic stable title across the completed scan result and fail immediately if the same title already exists under a different tag or commit, even when that conflicting object lives outside the current project's normal tag namespace. A draft or published stable release with that deterministic title is part of the same stable identity space; the design does not treat drafts as a separate namespace. If a pre-release GitHub Release exists for the same derived tag, the later direct `publish-github-official` job may promote it to a stable release only after remote asset identity checks compare every manifest-selected `github-release-asset`, including the required `SHA256SUMS` entry when GitHub Release assets are present, and confirm that every already-present remote asset matches the current local build output; a divergent same-tag pre-release is a hard failure. If a non-pre-release GitHub Release already exists for the same derived tag, defer the idempotent/no-op decision to the later direct `publish-github-official` job, which must verify remote asset identity before reporting success. If `github:official` is not in the resolved target set but stable GitHub Releases already exist for `release/<project-name>/v*`, the workflow may emit a non-blocking warning to the step summary reminding operators that those Releases are now manual state.
    - **Outputs:** `tag-name`, `language`, `project-name`, `project-path`, `version`, `release-line`, `targets` (compact JSON array of filtered official targets in canonical official-target order `nuget:official`, `npm:official`, `pypi:official`, `rubygems:official`, `github:official`), `nuget-auth-mechanism` (when `nuget:official` is selected), `rubygems-auth-mechanism` (when `rubygems:official` is selected), `npm-dist-tags` (compact JSON array when `npm:official` is selected), `npm-native-provenance-intent` (when `npm:official` is selected), `repository-visibility` (when `npm:official` is selected), and `npm-oidc-audience` (the frozen inventory `documentedOidcAudience` value for `npm:official`, currently `npm:registry.npmjs.org`).

4. **`static-analysis`**:
    - `needs: [resolve-context]`
    - `permissions: { contents: read }`
    - Checks out the source ref for this workflow run before enumerating files. Read-only checkout must use `persist-credentials: false`.
    - Restores the `mise` tool cache keyed by `mise.toml` and `mise.lock`, runs `mise install`, then runs `hk check <project-path>` scoped to the resolved project path. HK receives the project path directly and discovers applicable files under that path according to `hk.pkl`; this design does not pre-enumerate file names in shell.

5. **`clean-build`** (`build-csharp` / `build-python` / `build-jsts` / `build-ruby`):
    - For supply chain security, no prior artifacts are reused. A fresh build and test run is performed from the exact dispatch-selected commit for this workflow run. The checkout must use `fetch-depth: 0` for NBGV resolution.
    - The single language-matching official build job must run on a GitHub-hosted runner only. Self-hosted runners are unsupported because the produced artifact becomes the attested, provenance-gated input to every later official publish path.
    - Uses the same four static conditional build jobs pattern as `buddy.yml`. In `build-scope: release` mode, the single language-matching build job must request only `permissions: { contents: read }`, use `secrets: {}`, and receive the required `with:` inputs wired from `build-scope: release`, `needs.resolve-context.outputs.project-path`, `needs.resolve-context.outputs.project-name`, `checkout-ref: ${{ github.sha }}`, and `require-provenance: true`. Each build job depends on both `resolve-context` and `static-analysis`. Only the language-matching build job executes; the others are skipped. The matching release-mode build job must produce the exact manifest-selected publication files plus deterministic build-side verification inputs, but it must not mint OIDC tokens, generate attestation bundles, or execute any privileged publish logic.

6. **`attest-build-output`** (`attest-csharp` / `attest-python` / `attest-jsts` / `attest-ruby`):
    - `needs: [resolve-context, static-analysis, build-csharp, build-python, build-jsts, build-ruby]`
    - Uses the same four static conditional job pattern as the build stage. Only the language-matching top-level attestation caller executes; the others are skipped.
    - Each top-level attestation caller must invoke exactly one language-specific reusable workflow: `attest-csharp -> .github/workflows/_attest-build-csharp.yml`, `attest-python -> .github/workflows/_attest-build-python.yml`, `attest-jsts -> .github/workflows/_attest-build-jsts.yml`, and `attest-ruby -> .github/workflows/_attest-build-ruby.yml`. Those reusable workflow paths are part of the trusted verifier contract, not an implementation convenience.
    - Each top-level attestation caller job in `official.yml` must explicitly declare `permissions: { contents: read, id-token: write, attestations: write }`. The called reusable workflow must not declare any workflow-level or job-level `permissions:` block of its own; it inherits the caller job's grants under the reusable-workflow permission model defined earlier in this design.
    - The called reusable workflow must run on `ubuntu-latest`, use `secrets: {}`, perform a read-only checkout of the trusted control-plane code for `github.sha`, download the single language-matching build artifact, validate `artifact-manifest.json` and `build-verification-input.json`, and generate the attestation bundle set for the exact manifest-selected publication files.
    - Each called reusable workflow must contain exactly one attestation-producing job. That job's verified `job_workflow_ref` is the language-distinguishing signer identity consumed later by `require-provenance`; the repository must not collapse multiple languages back onto a single shared attestation workflow path.
    - The called reusable workflow must not perform dependency installation, package restore, test execution, or any shell evaluation of branch-controlled package metadata beyond manifest validation. Its only mutable external effect is generating GitHub artifact attestations for the already-built files.
    - The called reusable workflow must upload a second deterministic artifact named `provenance-output-<project-name>` that contains exactly `attestation-manifest.json` and the `attestations/` directory. Same-run overwrites use `overwrite: true`; cross-run reuse is unsupported.

7. **`require-provenance`**:
    - `needs: [preflight-check, resolve-context, static-analysis, build-csharp, build-python, build-jsts, build-ruby, attest-csharp, attest-python, attest-jsts, attest-ruby]`
    - `permissions: { contents: read, actions: read }`
    - `environment: production-evidence-write-<project-name>` — mandatory. Durable evidence persistence must occur only inside the dedicated evidence-write environment.
    - `if: always() && !cancelled() && !failure() && needs.resolve-context.result == 'success' && needs.static-analysis.result == 'success' && ((needs.resolve-context.outputs.language == 'csharp' && needs.build-csharp.result == 'success' && needs.attest-csharp.result == 'success' && needs.build-python.result == 'skipped' && needs.build-jsts.result == 'skipped' && needs.build-ruby.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-python.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-jsts.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-ruby.result == 'skipped') || (needs.resolve-context.outputs.language == 'python' && needs.build-csharp.result == 'skipped' && needs.build-python.result == 'success' && needs.build-jsts.result == 'skipped' && needs.build-ruby.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-csharp.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-python.result == 'success' && needs.attest-jsts.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-ruby.result == 'skipped') || (needs.resolve-context.outputs.language == 'jsts' && needs.build-csharp.result == 'skipped' && needs.build-python.result == 'skipped' && needs.build-jsts.result == 'success' && needs.build-ruby.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-csharp.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-python.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-jsts.result == 'success' && needs.attest-ruby.result == 'skipped') || (needs.resolve-context.outputs.language == 'ruby' && needs.build-csharp.result == 'skipped' && needs.build-python.result == 'skipped' && needs.build-jsts.result == 'skipped' && needs.build-ruby.result == 'success' && needs.attest-csharp.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-python.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-jsts.result == 'skipped' && needs.attest-ruby.result == 'success'))`
    - This job must not mint the environment-reader or ruleset-auditor GitHub App tokens and must not perform broad live control-plane API rechecks. The authoritative live gate for this job is the GitHub environment evaluation plus its own fail-closed environment-role check. Its first in-environment step must validate `CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE = evidence-write` before it mints the release-evidence writer App token or mutates durable evidence. A missing or wrong value is a hard failure and specifically covers the deleted-and-auto-recreated-environment path.
    - Before it mints the release-evidence writer token or mutates durable evidence, this job must also perform one synchronous revocation-and-admission recheck using only read-only repository APIs plus reviewed helper logic. That recheck must compare the current `refs/heads/main` state against `needs.preflight-check.outputs.main-control-plane-sha`, treat any intervening change to `.github/official-caller-refs.json`, `.github/official-dispatch-authorizers.json`, `.github/publish-trust-inventory.json`, `.github/provenance-signer-map.json`, `.github/release-recovery-ledger.jsonl`, or any `.github/release-recovery-ledger-archive-*.jsonl` file as revocation-sensitive, and re-evaluate the same-project completed-run blocker facts described in `preflight-check`, including unresolved `candidate-ledger-payload` `admissionBlock = true` artifacts and any other completed same-project run that reserved the official tag but lacks successful terminal reconciliation. If that narrow recheck fails, the job must hard-fail before credential mint or remote mutation instead of relying only on the asynchronous monitor to cancel the run later.
    - Before it downloads artifacts or runs any verifier helper, this job must perform two read-only checkouts in distinct directories: a frozen checkout of `needs.preflight-check.outputs.main-control-plane-sha` under `path: .ctrl-main` for `.github/provenance-signer-map.json` and any other non-executable control-plane state consumed by verification, plus a separate checkout of `github.sha` under `path: .release-src` for reviewed verifier helper code. The signer map used by this job must be read only from `.ctrl-main/.github/provenance-signer-map.json`, never from the branch-local workspace or from moving `main`. Executed helper code after this point may come only from `.release-src/` (or the equivalent primary checkout of `github.sha`); `.ctrl-main/` is data-only in this job.
    - This job does not use a repository-wide concurrency lock. Instead, after verification succeeds it must push to `refs/heads/release-evidence` with a bounded fetch/rebase/retry loop so concurrent official releases for different projects can append disjoint immutable paths without serializing the entire repository. Cross-project appends on that shared branch are normal steady-state behavior rather than evidence of corruption. The append budget is explicit: at most 5 push attempts with exponential backoff capped to the closed interval 2-8 seconds between attempts. If all 5 attempts are exhausted before the evidence commit is durably visible on `refs/heads/release-evidence`, the job must hard-fail before any anchor-tag update is attempted. It downloads the single language-matching build artifact plus `provenance-output-<project-name>`, validates `build-verification-input.json`, recomputes the SHA-256 of the downloaded `artifact-manifest.json`, validates the pre-generated `attestation-manifest.json`, verifies the deterministic `attestations/` layout, runs attestation verification against the attestation-job-generated bundles, and verifies binding to the exact attestation-job identity, repository identity, source commit, project identity, version, and build artifact manifest for this release attempt. The validation is exact: every manifest entry selected for publication must have exactly one attestation-manifest entry and exactly one matching bundle file, and no extra attestation-manifest entry or extra bundle file is allowed.
    - Mints a dedicated release-evidence writer GitHub App installation token and uses that token, not the job `GITHUB_TOKEN`, for the durable evidence push. The minted token must be masked immediately after issuance, before any other use, and should be explicitly revoked at job end on a best-effort basis.
    - `require-provenance` is the sole producer of the final durable `artifact-evidence.json`. The build and attestation jobs must not pre-populate any `verified*` field. After validation, this job must write an immutable evidence directory to the protected durable evidence branch at `.github/release-evidence/<project-name>/<version>/<source-commit>/runs/<github.run_id>-attempt-<github.run_attempt>/` containing exactly `artifact-evidence.json`, the copied `artifact-manifest.json`, the copied `build-verification-input.json`, the copied `attestation-manifest.json`, and the verified `attestations/` bundle files generated by the attestation job. Same-path overwrites are unsupported. After the evidence commit is pushed successfully, this job must also advance `refs/tags/control-plane/release-evidence-head/<project-name>` to the exact new evidence commit created for this run, and that commit must remain reachable from the current `refs/heads/release-evidence` tip. It must not require that the branch tip itself remain equal to one branch-global expected prior SHA, because concurrent cross-project appends on the shared `release-evidence` branch are permitted. GitHub's documented refs APIs let the workflow read a ref and later update it, but they do not expose a documented expected-old-SHA compare-and-swap parameter for this project-scoped anchor-tag update. Each attempt must therefore: (1) read the current project-scoped anchor target and the current `refs/heads/release-evidence` tip; (2) verify that the project-scoped anchor still matches the attempt's expected prior anchor for this project and that the specific new evidence commit for this run is reachable from the current branch tip; (3) perform the minimal non-destructive ref update supported by the reviewed writer path so the anchor points to that exact new evidence commit rather than to an unrelated later tip commit; and (4) reread both refs to prove that the anchor now points to the intended new evidence commit and that this commit still remains reachable from the current `release-evidence` tip. A newer branch tip caused only by another project's append is not a conflict by itself. Any unexpected same-project anchor movement or loss of reachability retries from the top of that loop rather than being described as a native CAS failure. The anchor-update budget is explicit: at most 3 attempts. That budget is intentional: after the same-project cross-ref admission checks, only unexpected concurrent mutation of that project's evidence anchor or loss of reachability for the newly written evidence commit should contend here, so exhausting the budget is treated as a control-plane anomaly rather than as normal load. If the evidence commit is already durable but the anchor cannot be advanced within those 3 attempts, the job must hard-fail with anchor-reconciliation semantics, must not emit success outputs, and `.github/workflows/official-run-health-monitor.yml` must open or update a `high-nonpage` incident immediately and escalate to `page` if the conflicting state overlaps another live official run for the same project or remains unreconciled for more than 5 minutes. This specific post-evidence / pre-anchor state has a lighter recovery path than emergency cleanup: when the durable evidence commit, expected evidence directory, and read-back verification are all intact, one release engineer may use a reviewed anchor-reconciliation helper under `eng/scripts/` with the release-evidence writer App to retry only the project-scoped anchor-tag update **only when that helper path remains a pure non-bypass fast-forward/update under the ordinary release-evidence writer authority**. That lighter path does not waive the repository's dual-control rule for bypass authority: if reconciliation would require any destructive ref mutation, any emergency-cleanup-group bypass, or any operation outside the reviewed release-evidence writer path, it immediately exits the anchor-only fast path and must follow the contemporaneous dual-control emergency-cleanup rules. Escalation to emergency cleanup is required only when the durable evidence commit itself is missing, divergent, otherwise fails integrity checks, or the anchor fix cannot be completed through that non-bypass helper path. The read-back verification must use the Git blobs API's content-addressed blob endpoints by blob SHA, not GitHub web URLs of the form `/blob/<blob-sha>/...`, and must verify byte equality for `artifact-evidence.json`, `artifact-manifest.json`, `build-verification-input.json`, and `attestation-manifest.json` before succeeding. This write path is mandatory, not best-effort. `artifactEvidenceUrl` for any later recovery ledger entry must point to the immutable Git blobs API URL of the committed `artifact-evidence.json`. A missing durable evidence branch, missing project-scoped anchor tag, evidence-writer credential failure, write failure, anchor-update failure, attempted overwrite, or byte-mismatch on the read-back verification is a hard failure.
    - Emits `artifact-evidence-url`, `artifact-manifest-sha256`, and `release-evidence-head-sha` as workflow outputs so later recovery and audit steps can reference the durable evidence record, exact verified manifest digest, and the reconciled project-scoped evidence-anchor commit directly. Despite the legacy output name, this value is the selected project's verified anchor commit, not a promise that the shared `refs/heads/release-evidence` tip itself stopped moving after this run.
    - This job is the machine-enforced production gate for Section 8. Until provenance support exists for every enabled official publish path, `require-provenance` must fail closed and keep `create-release-tag` plus all official publish jobs ineligible.

8. **`create-release-tag`**:
    - `needs: [resolve-context, static-analysis, build-csharp, build-python, build-jsts, build-ruby, require-provenance]`
    - `if: always() && !cancelled() && !failure() && needs.resolve-context.result == 'success' && needs.static-analysis.result == 'success' && needs.require-provenance.result == 'success'`
    - `permissions: { contents: read, actions: read }`
    - `environment: production-tag-write-<project-name>` — mandatory. Tag reservation must occur only inside the dedicated tag-write environment; package-registry and GitHub Release publish jobs must never enter that environment.
    - The job name and approval context shown to reviewers must include the project name, resolved version, caller ref, `github.run_id`, and at least a 12-character source-commit prefix so concurrent approval requests for the same project are distinguishable.
    - Mints a dedicated release-tag writer GitHub App installation token from a secret in `production-tag-write-<project-name>` and uses that token for the tag push. The job `GITHUB_TOKEN` is never the bypass actor for `refs/tags/release/**`. The minted token must be masked immediately after issuance, before any other use, and should be revoked explicitly at job end on a best-effort basis.
    - This job must not mint the environment-reader or ruleset-auditor GitHub App tokens and must not perform broad live control-plane API rechecks. The authoritative live gate for this job is the GitHub environment evaluation plus its own fail-closed environment-role check. Its first in-environment step must validate `CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE = tag-write` before it mints the release-tag writer App token or mutates any tag. A missing or wrong value is a hard failure and specifically covers the deleted-and-auto-recreated-environment path.
    - Before it mints the release-tag writer token or mutates any tag, this job must also perform the same synchronous revocation-and-admission recheck described for `require-provenance`, using the frozen `main-control-plane-sha` plus current read-only repository state to fail closed on revocation-sensitive `main` changes, unresolved same-project `candidate-ledger-payload` blockers, or another completed same-project official run that already reserved the tag and still lacks successful terminal reconciliation.
    - Creates the protected official release-identity tag `release/<project-name>/v<version>` at the current workflow commit after approval and before any official publish job becomes eligible. Reserving the official identity before per-destination publish is still intentional in this design; recovery rules for abandoned or partially used reservations are defined in Section 7.
    - **Tag creation logic:** If the tag does not exist, create it. If it already exists and points to the same commit, succeed as an idempotent no-op. If it exists but points to a different commit, fail immediately. There is no force path for official release tags. The existence check must query the remote protected tag namespace via `git ls-remote --tags` or the GitHub refs API; when `git ls-remote --tags` is used, annotated tags must be compared by their peeled `refs/tags/<tag>^{}` commit SHA rather than by the raw tag-object SHA. A local `git tag -l` view from checkout is insufficient and must not be the sole source of truth. If the create attempt returns a duplicate or conflict response such as HTTP `422`, the job must re-query the remote tag state immediately and treat the result as `no-op` only when the just-observed remote tag now points to the same source commit; otherwise it is a hard failure.
    - Checks out the current source ref read-only, then configures git explicitly to push with the minted GitHub App installation token. The job must not persist the default `GITHUB_TOKEN` as a write-capable remote credential.
    - Emits a machine-readable workflow output `tag-result` whose value is exactly `created` or `no-op`, uploads an immutable same-run artifact `tag-reservation-result-<project-name>` containing a compact JSON record with `projectName`, `version`, `tagName`, `sourceCommit`, and `tagResult`, and appends a one-line summary to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` describing the reserved release identity, caller ref, source commit, and tag outcome.

9. **Publish jobs** (static conditional, one job per official ecosystem-destination pair):
    - Uses the same per-destination split structure as `buddy.yml`, but official targets now include `github:official` in addition to the production package registries. Unlike buddy, official publish jobs do not need to restate the full language-matching build predicate in each `if:` guard because `require-provenance` already enforces the exact single-build-success pattern for the resolved language, and `create-release-tag` plus all official publish jobs are blocked on `require-provenance` success.
    - `needs: [resolve-context, static-analysis, build-csharp, build-python, build-jsts, build-ruby, require-provenance, create-release-tag]`
    - `environment:` is **mandatory**, not optional, and must be target-specific: both `publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher` and `publish-nuget-official-api-key` use `production-nuget-<project-name>`, `publish-npm-official` uses `production-npm-<project-name>`, `publish-pypi-official` uses `production-pypi-<project-name>`, both `publish-rubygems-official-trusted-publisher` and `publish-rubygems-official-api-key` use `production-rubygems-<project-name>`, and `publish-github-official` uses `production-github-<project-name>`. This enables human approval gates and target-local OIDC environment claims.
    - Every environment-gated publish job name and first summary line must include the target name, project name, resolved version, caller ref, `github.run_id`, and at least a 12-character source-commit prefix so concurrent approval requests for the same project are distinguishable in the approval UI and in notifications.
    - `publish-npm-official` and `publish-pypi-official` use `permissions: { contents: read, actions: read, id-token: write }` for trusted publishing. `publish-rubygems-official-trusted-publisher` uses `permissions: { contents: read, actions: read, id-token: write }`, while `publish-rubygems-official-api-key` uses `permissions: { contents: read, actions: read }`. Those two RubyGems jobs are mutually exclusive and must be selected strictly from the frozen `needs.resolve-context.outputs.rubygems-auth-mechanism` value. `publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher` uses `permissions: { contents: read, actions: read, id-token: write }`, while `publish-nuget-official-api-key` uses `permissions: { contents: read, actions: read }`. Those two NuGet jobs are mutually exclusive and must be selected strictly from the frozen `needs.resolve-context.outputs.nuget-auth-mechanism` value. Here the terminology is exact: `api-key-secret` is the inventory `authMechanism` label, while `NUGET_FALLBACK_API_KEY` and `RUBYGEMS_FALLBACK_API_KEY` are the protected-environment secrets that implement that mechanism. `nuget:official` and `rubygems:official` each remain one logical target across `targets`, `confirm-publish-state`, recovery classification, and `release-complete`; only the direct job wiring is split for least privilege, so every target-to-job mapping outside the immediate publish step must continue to collapse each pair back into its single logical target. When the frozen inventory entry selects `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, only `publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher` may run, it must invoke `NuGet/login@v1` or a reviewed successor and use the approved `NUGET_USER` path, and `publish-nuget-official-api-key` must remain `result == "skipped"`. When the frozen inventory entry selects `authMechanism = api-key-secret`, only `publish-nuget-official-api-key` may run, it must skip `NuGet/login@v1`, must not request or consume an OIDC token, and must rely only on the protected-environment `NUGET_FALLBACK_API_KEY`, while `publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher` must remain `result == "skipped"`. When the frozen inventory entry selects `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, only `publish-rubygems-official-trusted-publisher` may run, it must rely on the reviewed OIDC-backed path, and `publish-rubygems-official-api-key` must remain `result == "skipped"`. When the frozen inventory entry selects `authMechanism = api-key-secret`, only `publish-rubygems-official-api-key` may run, it must skip any OIDC request entirely, must rely only on the protected-environment `RUBYGEMS_FALLBACK_API_KEY`, and `publish-rubygems-official-trusted-publisher` must remain `result == "skipped"`. Both direct NuGet jobs must pass the unchanged frozen `needs.resolve-context.outputs.nuget-auth-mechanism` value into `.github/actions/publish-nuget-official`, and both the direct job and the composite action must treat any mismatch between that frozen value and the environment-scoped credential shape as a hard failure. Both direct RubyGems jobs must pass the unchanged frozen `needs.resolve-context.outputs.rubygems-auth-mechanism` value into `.github/actions/publish-rubygems-official`, and both the direct job and the composite action must treat any mismatch between that frozen value and the environment-scoped credential shape as a hard failure. On the trusted-publisher path, the direct job or helper must treat `steps.<login-step-id>.outputs.NUGET_API_KEY` as the only valid short-lived credential source and must remap it immediately to a non-conflicting variable such as `NUGET_OIDC_API_KEY` before the push step. On the RubyGems trusted-publisher path, `RUBYGEMS_FALLBACK_API_KEY` must be absent; on the RubyGems `api-key-secret` path, trusted-publisher selector inputs must be absent and the direct job must expose only `GEM_HOST_API_KEY` to the final `gem push` helper. All seven official publish jobs (counting the split NuGet and RubyGems pairs) run directly inside `official.yml`; `publish-github-official` uses `permissions: { contents: write, actions: read }`, which already satisfies read access. Reviewed local composite actions may still perform shared artifact validation, helper logic, or the final target mutation command, provided they are invoked as steps inside those direct `official.yml` jobs after the job-level environment and permission gates are already in force. Reusable-workflow indirection for official publication remains forbidden. In particular, `publish-pypi-official` must invoke `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` directly from `official.yml`; local composite actions or scripts may prepare artifact layout or post-process results, but must not wrap the upstream trusted-publishing step.
    - Every direct official publish job must declare `runs-on: ubuntu-latest` explicitly in the concrete workflow YAML. This is not just syntactic completeness for ordinary jobs: the reviewed `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` path is GNU/Linux-only and smoke-tested on GitHub-provided Ubuntu VMs, and the rest of the direct official publish examples in this design standardize on the same GitHub-hosted Ubuntu baseline.
    - Every selected official publish path must expose a terminal-gate-visible `publish-result` output. Direct jobs must map their step or composite-action outputs to job outputs explicitly, and `publish-npm-official` must also map `applied-dist-tags`, `npm-native-provenance-classification`, and `resolved-package-access`. Both NuGet jobs must surface the same `publish-result` contract so `confirm-publish-state` and `release-complete` can consume whichever one actually ran. Step summaries alone are insufficient.
    - Because `official.yml` may run only from the protected control-plane branch set, no separate runtime assertion is required here to distinguish the caller branch from the trusted control-plane source. The target-specific production environment branch policy and branch protections carry that responsibility.
    - Direct official publish jobs do not declare a job-level `secrets:` map. They rely on explicit job `permissions`, OIDC, and target-specific protected environments; blanket secret inheritance remains prohibited.
    - Official publish jobs must not mint the environment-reader or ruleset-auditor GitHub App tokens and must not perform broad live control-plane API rechecks. The authoritative live gate for these jobs is the GitHub environment evaluation plus their own fail-closed environment-role check. Each selected publish job's first in-environment step must validate the exact expected `CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE` value before it requests OIDC or mutates any remote target. A missing or wrong value is a hard failure and specifically covers the deleted-and-auto-recreated-environment path. Before it requests OIDC, consumes an api-key fallback secret, or mutates any remote target, each selected publish job must also perform the same synchronous revocation-and-admission recheck described for `require-provenance`, using its read-only `actions: read` plus repository-read scope to fail closed on revocation-sensitive `main` changes, unresolved same-project `candidate-ledger-payload` blockers, or another completed same-project official run that already reserved the official tag and still lacks successful terminal reconciliation.
    - Before any registry mutation, each official publish job must recompute the SHA-256 of the downloaded `artifact-manifest.json` and verify that it exactly matches both the local `build-verification-input.json` value and `require-provenance.outputs.artifact-manifest-sha256`. Self-consistency of the downloaded artifact alone is insufficient.
    - Each publish step uses idempotent publish logic from the protected control-plane branch set. Duplicate-version outcomes (`409`, `422`, or tool-equivalent "already exists" responses) count as success only after the workflow verifies the target-specific remote identity contract. For `nuget:official`, raw downloaded `.nupkg` bytes are explicitly **not** a valid idempotency proof because NuGet.org repository-signs packages after upload; idempotency must instead be based on exact package ID/version presence, optional `.snupkg` presence, and the same reserved release identity. If the `.nupkg` is already present but the expected `.snupkg` is still missing remotely, the rerun performs the missing symbol upload and must emit `publish-result = new-publish`; `publish-result = no-op` is allowed only when both the primary package and the expected symbol-package state are already fully reconciled. For `pypi:official`, a state where only the wheel or only the sdist exists is an explicit partial-publish incident state, not a success and not a generic `not found`. `prepare-pypi-official` must classify that state as `publish-plan = partial-recovery`, must place only the missing distribution files into `packages-dir`, and `publish-pypi-official` must invoke `pypa/gh-action-pypi-publish` with `skip-existing: true` so reruns can finish the same release identity without failing on the already-present file set. `publish-result = no-op` is valid for PyPI only when both the expected wheel and the expected sdist are already present remotely. For `npm:official`, idempotency must additionally distinguish immutable package-version presence from mutable moving-tag state. If the exact package version is already present and every requested tag in `npm-dist-tags` still points to that version, the rerun is a normal npm no-op. If the exact package version is already present but a requested **stable moving tag** (`latest` or `release-v<major>.<minor>`) has already advanced to a strictly higher stable version within that same deterministic tag family, the rerun must not move that tag backward; that state is still an idempotent npm no-op for the older release identity rather than a permanent recovery failure. A requested npm tag pointing to a lower version, to a prerelease when the requested family is stable, or to an unrelated family remains a hard mismatch. For RubyGems and GitHub Releases, the workflow verifies the already-published remote artifact set against the local artifact set and the target-specific identity rules below. Authentication failures, authorization failures, malformed artifacts, and upstream `5xx` or transport failures remain hard failures after a bounded in-run retry policy. Every publish path in this design must retry transient network or upstream `5xx` failures at least three times with exponential backoff before surfacing failure, must use an initial delay of at least 5 seconds, a backoff multiplier of at least 2x, and a per-attempt request timeout of at most 30 seconds, and must not spin indefinitely or cross the job timeout budget.

    Illustrative fragment only; this block is a workflow logic sketch, not standalone valid YAML.

    ```text
    publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher:
        needs: [resolve-context, static-analysis, build-csharp, build-python, build-jsts, build-ruby, require-provenance, create-release-tag]
        outputs:
            publish-result: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.publish-result }}
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
            contents: read
            actions: read
            id-token: write
        environment:
            name: production-nuget-${{ needs.resolve-context.outputs.project-name }}
        if: |
            always() && !cancelled() && !failure() &&
            needs.resolve-context.result == 'success' &&
            needs.static-analysis.result == 'success' &&
            needs.require-provenance.result == 'success' &&
            needs.create-release-tag.result == 'success' &&
            needs.resolve-context.outputs.nuget-auth-mechanism == 'trusted-publisher' &&
            contains(fromJson(needs.resolve-context.outputs.targets || '[]'), 'nuget:official')
        steps:
            - name: Verify environment role
              shell: bash
              env:
                  CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE: ${{ vars.CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE }}
              run: |
                  [[ "$CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE" == "publish-nuget" ]] || { echo "expected CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE=publish-nuget"; exit 1; }
            - name: Checkout trusted control-plane code
              uses: actions/checkout@<sha>
              with:
                  ref: ${{ github.sha }}
                  fetch-depth: 1
                  persist-credentials: false
            - id: publish
              name: Publish to NuGet.org via trusted publishing
              uses: ./.github/actions/publish-nuget-official
              with:
                  artifact-name: build-output-${{ needs.resolve-context.outputs.project-name }}
                  artifact-manifest-sha256: ${{ needs.require-provenance.outputs.artifact-manifest-sha256 }}
                  auth-mechanism: ${{ needs.resolve-context.outputs.nuget-auth-mechanism }}
                  version: ${{ needs.resolve-context.outputs.version }}

    publish-nuget-official-api-key:
        needs: [resolve-context, static-analysis, build-csharp, build-python, build-jsts, build-ruby, require-provenance, create-release-tag]
        outputs:
            publish-result: ${{ steps.publish.outputs.publish-result }}
        runs-on: ubuntu-latest
        permissions:
            contents: read
            actions: read
        environment:
            name: production-nuget-${{ needs.resolve-context.outputs.project-name }}
        if: |
            always() && !cancelled() && !failure() &&
            needs.resolve-context.result == 'success' &&
            needs.static-analysis.result == 'success' &&
            needs.require-provenance.result == 'success' &&
            needs.create-release-tag.result == 'success' &&
            needs.resolve-context.outputs.nuget-auth-mechanism == 'api-key-secret' &&
            contains(fromJson(needs.resolve-context.outputs.targets || '[]'), 'nuget:official')
        steps:
            - name: Verify environment role
              shell: bash
              env:
                  CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE: ${{ vars.CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE }}
              run: |
                  [[ "$CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE" == "publish-nuget" ]] || { echo "expected CONTROL_PLANE_ENVIRONMENT_ROLE=publish-nuget"; exit 1; }
            - name: Checkout trusted control-plane code
              uses: actions/checkout@<sha>
              with:
                  ref: ${{ github.sha }}
                  fetch-depth: 1
                  persist-credentials: false
            - id: publish
              name: Publish to NuGet.org via reviewed api-key fallback
              uses: ./.github/actions/publish-nuget-official
              with:
                  artifact-name: build-output-${{ needs.resolve-context.outputs.project-name }}
                  artifact-manifest-sha256: ${{ needs.require-provenance.outputs.artifact-manifest-sha256 }}
                  auth-mechanism: ${{ needs.resolve-context.outputs.nuget-auth-mechanism }}
                  version: ${{ needs.resolve-context.outputs.version }}

    ```

    The workflow logic sketch above shows the direct `nuget:official` split-job shape. Exactly one of the two jobs may run in any given official attempt, and the non-selected job must remain `result == "skipped"`. When `authMechanism = trusted-publisher`, the direct trusted-publisher job and `.github/actions/publish-nuget-official` must assert that `NUGET_USER` is present and `NUGET_FALLBACK_API_KEY` is absent before invoking `NuGet/login@v1` or its reviewed successor. Because `NuGet/login@v1` exposes the temporary key as `steps.<login-step-id>.outputs.NUGET_API_KEY`, the trusted-publisher path must immediately remap that value to a non-conflicting variable such as `NUGET_OIDC_API_KEY` before `dotnet nuget push`; ambient `$NUGET_FALLBACK_API_KEY` is reserved for the fallback secret path and must never be read on the trusted-publisher path. When the frozen inventory instead selects `authMechanism = api-key-secret`, only the direct api-key job may run; it must assert that `NUGET_FALLBACK_API_KEY` is present, must assert that `NUGET_USER` is absent, must skip `NuGet/login@v1`, must not request or consume an OIDC token, and must invoke the reviewed `dotnet nuget push --api-key` path against the same downloaded artifact and manifest-validation contract. The fallback job never declares `id-token: write`, and repository policy must treat any api-key-path OIDC use as a hard failure.

10. **`confirm-publish-state`**:
    - `needs: [resolve-context, static-analysis, build-csharp, build-python, build-jsts, build-ruby, require-provenance, create-release-tag, publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher, publish-nuget-official-api-key, publish-npm-official, publish-pypi-official, publish-rubygems-official-trusted-publisher, publish-rubygems-official-api-key, publish-github-official]`
    - `if: always() && !cancelled() && needs.resolve-context.result == 'success' && needs.static-analysis.result == 'success' && needs.require-provenance.result == 'success' && needs.create-release-tag.result == 'success'`
    - `permissions: { contents: read }`
    - Before any confirmation logic runs, this job must check out the repository read-only with `persist-credentials: false`, restore the `mise` tool cache keyed by `mise.toml` plus `mise.lock`, and run `mise install` so any jq-based normalization uses the reviewed locked toolchain rather than the runner image.
    - This job is intentionally one ordinary job, not a matrix or reusable-workflow fan-out. Parallel confirmation must therefore happen **inside** this single job. The reviewed implementation pattern is strict and must use three in-job phases: (1) a preparation phase that normalizes the selected logical targets and creates deterministic per-target scratch directories under one workspace-local root; (2) one reviewed supervisor step that launches one bounded worker subprocess per selected logical target, explicitly unsets `GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `GITHUB_ENV`, and `GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` for every worker before `exec`, and starts each worker in its own new session/process group (for example via `setsid` or an equivalent reviewed launcher) so timeout cleanup can target the worker group without sharing a process group with the supervisor; those launches must also be OS-level bounded rather than relying only on application-request timeouts, so the reviewed launcher must be process-group-aware and equivalent in effect to `timeout W setsid <worker-entrypoint>`, where `W` is no greater than that target's confirmation budget and the worker manifest records the resulting process-group-capable cleanup handle before the supervisor enters `wait`. Application-level per-request timeouts are still required, but they are not sufficient on their own: the OS-level timeout must be able to kill the whole worker process group when a TCP connect/read stall or other kernel-level hang would otherwise leave the supervisor blocked indefinitely. The recorded worker manifest must therefore keep process-group-capable cleanup data (for example target name, pid or process-group ID, deadline, scratch path, and completion-marker path), with a plain pid retained only for diagnostics when both are recorded. Those workers are concurrent children of the supervisor step, not cross-step detached workers: the supervisor must perform an explicit shell `wait` or reviewed equivalent join for **every** launched worker before that step exits, must normalize raw exit or timeout conditions into per-target status files while itself exiting `0`, and must attempt same-step cleanup for every launched worker group before step completion; if the reducer later lacks proof that a worker was joined or cleaned up as designed, that missing proof is an infrastructure anomaly rather than silent success; and (3) one reducer step with `if: always()` that is the **only** step allowed to write job outputs, checkpoint artifacts, or step-summary checkpoints. Incremental checkpoint emission is reducer-only as well: during that single reducer execution it may iterate over the normalized target states, rewrite `confirm-publish-state-checkpoint.json`, and append one-line JSON checkpoint updates to `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` after each larger confirmed-target batch or semantic-state transition derived from the supervisor's normalized results. Those checkpoint writes are therefore batch-visible only during reducer execution after worker collection; this one-job architecture does **not** provide realtime worker-time checkpoint visibility. Achieving true realtime confirmation checkpoints would require a different multi-step or periodic-polling architecture and is out of scope for this design. That reducer-only allowance is explicit and does **not** permit worker-time writes. Workers may read a shared checkout, but they must write only inside their own per-target scratch directory; direct concurrent writes from workers to `$GITHUB_OUTPUT`, `$GITHUB_ENV`, or `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` are forbidden. Because reviewed GitHub documentation covers step-level process isolation and per-step workflow-command files but does **not** document a guarantee that detached background processes survive across step boundaries on GitHub-hosted runners, this design forbids cross-step detached-worker joins for confirmation. Launch, supervision, timeout handling, and collection must stay inside the same reviewed parent step, where shell `wait` and same-step process-group cleanup are supported. Completion markers in scratch remain the durable per-target handoff from that supervisor step to the later reducer step; later steps must consume only the normalized scratch results rather than attempt to rejoin worker processes. Worker exit codes influence only the reducer's computed semantic state, not the job conclusion. Only infrastructure failure that prevents the reducer from running or emitting outputs may make the job itself fail. A job-level timeout that GitHub enforces while the supervisor step is still running is one such infrastructure failure: the reducer step never starts, no confirmation outputs are emitted, and operators must follow recovery step 11 rather than assuming `if: always()` can override a hard job termination. In other words, this design depends only on documented per-step runner/process isolation plus same-step shell control flow, not on any undocumented guarantee that background workers remain joinable after a later step starts.
    - Re-queries every selected official target from `fromJson(needs.resolve-context.outputs.targets)` against its live remote system and emits `confirmed-published-targets` as a compact ordered JSON array in canonical official-target order, serialized exactly as compact JSON equivalent to `jq -c`. It must also emit `confirmation-state` with the closed set `{complete, partial-timeout, partial-upstream-failure}`, `confirmation-mode` with the closed set `{parallel, serial-degraded}`, and `confirmation-alert` with the closed set `{none, serial-degraded}`. These semantic states are workflow outputs rather than job conclusions: once the reducer can emit well-formed outputs, it is the job's always-success boundary and must exit `0` for all three `confirmation-state` values so downstream gates and recovery logic can read the outputs. Only a hard timeout, runner crash, malformed reducer input, or other infrastructure failure that prevents reliable output emission should make the job itself fail. Because job outputs are not reliable after a hard timeout, this job must also persist the latest checkpoint as both a machine-readable `confirm-publish-state-checkpoint.json` artifact (same-run overwrite allowed) and a one-line JSON checkpoint in `$GITHUB_STEP_SUMMARY` whenever the reducer observes a larger confirmed-target batch than the last emitted checkpoint or settles a new semantic state. The reducer's **first** summary line must also be a compact terminal-status JSON object that includes at least `confirmationState`, `confirmationMode`, `confirmationAlert`, and `confirmedPublishedTargets`, so operators and downstream parsing logic see any degraded-mode anomaly immediately instead of only in free-form prose. When `confirmation-alert != none`, the reducer must additionally emit a GitHub `::error::` annotation that names the anomaly while still exiting `0`, so the workflow has an unmistakable hard-failure-style signal even when correctness was preserved. Those checkpoint writes occur only during reducer execution after collector normalization; they are recovery hints for batch progress, not realtime worker-time telemetry. `confirmed-published-targets` is authoritative only on full job success; the checkpoint artifact plus summary are recovery hints and never substitute for the required full confirmation. Result collection may happen in parallel, but final serialization must sort explicitly into canonical official-target order before emission; completion order must never leak into the output array. This job is the authoritative workflow-side source of truth for `publishedTargets`; machine-readable publish outputs and step summaries are diagnostic hints only. It must still run after a selected publish job fails so the workflow captures the best available live remote state for partial-publish recovery; in that case `confirmation-state` must settle to `partial-upstream-failure` unless every selected target was nevertheless confirmed. A successful run that emits `confirmation-alert = serial-degraded` is therefore not merely noisy success: it is a project-scoped control-plane discrepancy that must later create a blocking recovery-ledger audit before the same project is release-eligible again.
    - Remote confirmation must use bounded retry with backoff to absorb registry eventual consistency. A single immediate `not found` response after a publish attempt is `unknown`, not authoritative absence. The reviewed steady-state design is parallel confirmation inside one job. This design also approves one degraded fallback `confirmation-mode = serial-degraded` inside that same job, but only when the supervisor proves that it could not establish the reviewed worker model **before any isolated worker was launched and before any target-specific remote confirmation began**. Serial degradation is therefore a start-of-job architecture fallback, not a mid-flight repair path: once at least one reviewed worker has launched successfully, any later worker-launch problem, worker exit failure, or worker-timeout condition must remain inside `confirmation-mode = parallel` and settle through `confirmation-state` plus per-target normalized results rather than silently converting the whole job into serial mode. In degraded mode the job must confirm the selected logical targets serially, preserve the same canonical target ordering and per-target semantics, emit `confirmation-mode = serial-degraded` plus `confirmation-alert = serial-degraded`, emit the reducer `::error::` annotation described above, and raise a `high-nonpage` control-plane incident so the worker model is repaired before the next routine release. The fallback is approved because correctness is higher priority than the normal parallel latency target, but it is not silent: a serial-degraded confirmation is a control-plane anomaly, not the new steady state. The later terminal success path must therefore create or update one blocking `audit` ledger record with `scope = "control-plane-monitoring-project"`, matching `projectName`, `result = "discrepancy-found"`, `followUpStatus = "required-open"`, `evidenceUrl` pointing to the workflow run URL, and `nextReviewAt` no later than 24 hours after the run; fresh official dispatches for that same project remain blocked until a later audit revision reconciles or resolves that discrepancy. The periodic `confirm-publish-state` architecture self-test and any same-change worker-model redesign evidence must explicitly validate that trigger boundary: serial degradation is legal only when zero workers launched, and any design that allows a later single-worker failure to masquerade as serial-degraded is invalid. Each selected target must be retried at least three times with increasing delays, use an initial delay of at least 30 seconds, a backoff multiplier of at least 2x, and a per-request timeout of at most 30 seconds. The maximum confirmation budget is 10 minutes per selected target except `github:official`, which receives 15 minutes because it must fetch durable-evidence blobs plus the remote `SHA256SUMS` asset, and `pypi:official`, which receives 20 minutes to accommodate slower index convergence.
    - For `nuget:official`, confirmation must first determine whether a symbol package is expected for this release identity by fetching `require-provenance.outputs.artifact-evidence-url` through the Git Blobs API, following `artifactManifestBlobApiUrl`, and reading the durable `artifact-manifest.json` from the evidence branch. If that manifest contains any `package` entry whose `path` ends with `.snupkg`, symbol publication is expected; otherwise it is not. Confirmation must then query the flat-container or equivalent package-content endpoint for the exact primary package/version identity and, when symbol publication is expected, must also confirm `.snupkg` presence through the documented NuGet.org symbol-server download base `https://symbols.nuget.org/download/symbols`, using the exact id/version-derived symbol path that the reviewed publish helper emits for that identity. Search-index visibility, package-details pages, and generic symbol search are advisory only and must not be the blocking confirmation signal. If the remote state ever shows `.snupkg` present while the corresponding primary `.nupkg` is absent, that is an inconsistent reverse-partial state and must be treated as a hard confirmation failure rather than as idempotent success or as a recoverable symbol-only no-op.
    - For `pypi:official`, confirmation must query `/pypi/<project>/<version>/json`, enumerate `urls[*].filename`, and require at least one `.whl` plus at least one `.tar.gz` file before confirming publication. Version existence alone is insufficient.
    - For `npm:official`, this job must also verify the ordered requested `dist-tags` array emitted by `resolve-context`. The default confirmation semantic is requested-tag subset inclusion: every tag named in `npm-dist-tags` must currently point to the selected version, but extra registry tags outside that requested array are tolerated by this check and must not cause failure solely because the registry exposes a larger tag set for the same version. The registry-side dist-tag payload is an object keyed by tag name, so this job must first project that object onto the requested tag set, preserve the request order emitted by `resolve-context`, and compare only that ordered projection; raw object-vs-array equality is invalid, and exact equality against the version's entire registry tag set is not the rule. There is one reviewed exception for stable moving-tag supersession: when the selected release identity is itself a stable npm release and a requested tag is either `latest` or `release-v<major>.<minor>`, confirmation may still classify the target as successfully published when the selected version is present but that requested tag now points to a strictly higher stable version in the same deterministic tag family. That superseded-by-higher-version path is a recovery-safe no-op for the older release identity because this design forbids moving stable npm tags backward. It does **not** apply when the requested tag points to a lower version, a prerelease version, or a different deterministic tag family. The same job must also consume `publish-npm-official.outputs.npm-native-provenance-classification` plus `publish-npm-official.outputs.resolved-package-access` and treat both as closed-set contracts. `resolved-package-access` must be exactly `public` or `restricted`, and it is the authoritative same-run package-access fact for npm-native-provenance validation in `confirm-publish-state`; this reducer must fail closed if that output is missing or malformed instead of recomputing the gating truth from a possibly drifted post-publish read path. `needs.resolve-context.outputs.repository-visibility` is likewise the authoritative same-run repository-visibility fact for that validation and must be present with one of `{public, private}` whenever `npm:official` is selected. Read-only npm metadata or tarball inspection may still be used as diagnostic evidence when operators investigate a mismatch, but that later evidence must not silently override the workflow-emitted same-run access fact. If the classification is `expected`, confirmation must treat missing npm-native provenance as a target-level confirmation failure after the package metadata has converged. If the classification is `intentionally-disabled`, confirmation must additionally require `needs.resolve-context.outputs.npm-native-provenance-intent == 'disabled'` and must verify that `needs.resolve-context.outputs.repository-visibility` plus `resolved-package-access` would otherwise have made npm native provenance expected; `disabled` must not override an objective `not-applicable-*` state. If the classification is `not-applicable-private-repository`, `not-applicable-private-package`, or `not-applicable-private-repository-and-package`, confirmation must not wait for npm-native provenance to appear, but it must still verify that the emitted classification matches `needs.resolve-context.outputs.repository-visibility` and the same-run `resolved-package-access` fact.
    - For `rubygems:official`, confirmation must query the RubyGems versions API or an equivalent version-specific endpoint for the exact gem name/version identity and confirm that the released `.gem` payload metadata matches the manifest-selected artifact set; website search visibility is advisory only. When the provider response exposes an explicit `yanked: true` flag for that exact version, confirmation must treat the target as not successfully published for same-version recovery purposes and must not classify it as idempotently present.
    - For `github:official`, confirmation must query the GitHub Releases API for the exact reserved tag, verify that the release title remains `<project-name> v<version>`, verify the expected prerelease/stable state, require the exact manifest-selected GitHub Release asset set including `SHA256SUMS`, and reject any unexpected extra asset. Its expected digest source is the durable evidence only: the confirmation worker must fetch `require-provenance.outputs.artifact-evidence-url` through the Git blobs API, follow `artifactManifestBlobApiUrl` from that evidence document to obtain the expected manifest-selected release-asset digests, and must not re-download the CI build artifact as a second source of truth. It must then download the remote `SHA256SUMS` release asset, verify that `SHA256SUMS` itself is an expected manifest-selected release asset, cross-check the `SHA256SUMS` contents against the durable-evidence digest set, and verify that every remote asset digest matches that same durable evidence before confirming publication.

11. **`release-complete`**:
    - `needs: [resolve-context, static-analysis, build-csharp, build-python, build-jsts, build-ruby, attest-csharp, attest-python, attest-jsts, attest-ruby, require-provenance, create-release-tag, publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher, publish-nuget-official-api-key, publish-npm-official, publish-pypi-official, publish-rubygems-official-trusted-publisher, publish-rubygems-official-api-key, publish-github-official, confirm-publish-state]`
    - `if: always()`
    - `permissions: { contents: read }`
    - Before the jq assertion runs, this job must check out the repository read-only with `persist-credentials: false`, restore the `mise` tool cache keyed by `mise.toml` plus `mise.lock`, and run `mise install` so the jq gate uses the reviewed locked toolchain rather than the runner image.
    - Performs the terminal correctness check for official releases. It must first assert that `resolve-context.result == "success"`, `static-analysis.result == "success"`, `require-provenance.result == "success"`, `create-release-tag.result == "success"`, and `confirm-publish-state.result == "success"`. It must also assert that `create-release-tag.outputs.tag-result` is present and equal to `created` or `no-op`, that `require-provenance.outputs.artifact-evidence-url` is present and non-empty, that `require-provenance.outputs.release-evidence-head-sha` is present and non-empty, that `confirm-publish-state.outputs.confirmation-state == "complete"`, and that `confirm-publish-state.outputs.confirmation-alert` is present with one of `{none, serial-degraded}`. `require-provenance.outputs.release-evidence-head-sha` is the project-scoped evidence-anchor commit for the reconciled durable evidence state, not a claim that the shared `release-evidence` branch tip itself is frozen. It must then parse `targets` as JSON, assert that the filtered target set is non-empty, map that set to the exact publish jobs `{nuget:official -> exactly one of publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher or publish-nuget-official-api-key, npm:official -> publish-npm-official, pypi:official -> publish-pypi-official, rubygems:official -> exactly one of publish-rubygems-official-trusted-publisher or publish-rubygems-official-api-key, github:official -> publish-github-official}`, and assert that every selected target finished with `result == "success"` and a valid `publish-result` output in `{new-publish, no-op}`.
    - It must also assert that every non-selected publish job finished with `result == "skipped"`. For `nuget:official`, that means exactly one of the two NuGet jobs must be `result == "success"` and the other must be `result == "skipped"`; when `nuget:official` is not selected, both NuGet jobs must be `result == "skipped"`. For `rubygems:official`, that means exactly one of the two RubyGems jobs must be `result == "success"` and the other must be `result == "skipped"`; when `rubygems:official` is not selected, both RubyGems jobs must be `result == "skipped"`.
    - It must also assert that `confirm-publish-state.outputs.confirmed-published-targets` parses as JSON and exactly equals the selected target array in canonical order. When `confirm-publish-state.outputs.confirmation-alert == "serial-degraded"`, `release-complete` must repeat the same compact anomaly JSON in its own first summary line, emit a matching `::error::` annotation before continuing, and trigger the reviewed recovery-ledger update path so `.github/release-recovery-ledger.jsonl` receives or updates the blocking project-scoped audit described in Section 7. A final green terminal gate must never hide that anomaly from humans, downstream parsers, or later admission control.
    - Any `release-complete` path that must create or update ledger state — including `confirmation-alert = serial-degraded` and a successful `npm-native-provenance-classification = intentionally-disabled` path — must do so only through the reviewed PR-based ledger-update trigger. `release-complete` itself must not push `.github/release-recovery-ledger.jsonl` directly; instead it must materialize exactly one compact `candidate-ledger-payload.json` file, upload it as the immutable artifact `candidate-ledger-payload-<project-name>-<github.run_id>-attempt-<github.run_attempt>`, and record the run evidence that later materializes into the minimal reviewed PR against `main`. That payload is not schema-free logging: it must contain the exact proposed `recordType`, the exact proposed `auditId` or `incidentId`, `projectName`, `releaseLine` when applicable, `evidenceUrl`, and a boolean `admissionBlock`. For `confirmation-alert = serial-degraded`, `admissionBlock` must be `true` and the payload must describe the exact blocking `audit.scope = control-plane-monitoring-project` record that `preflight-check` later consumes immediately as a temporary fail-closed admission fact even before the reviewed PR is opened or merged. For a successful `npm-native-provenance-classification = intentionally-disabled` path, `admissionBlock` must be `false` because that required `single-release-identity` audit is durable evidence rather than a same-project dispatch block. This is a terminal-gate precondition rather than best-effort logging: when `confirmation-alert = serial-degraded` or a successful `npm-native-provenance-classification = intentionally-disabled` requires a ledger update, `release-complete` must hard-fail if that candidate payload file is absent, malformed, missing its exact proposed record ID or `admissionBlock` field, or not uploaded under the required artifact name; when no ledger update is required, that artifact must be absent.
    - If `npm:official` is selected, it must also assert that both `publish-npm-official.outputs.applied-dist-tags` and `resolve-context.outputs.npm-dist-tags` are present, parse as JSON arrays, and are exactly equal in canonical order.
    - It must also assert that the single language-matching build job finished with `result == "success"`; the three non-matching build jobs must be `result == "skipped"`.
    - It must also assert that the single language-matching attestation job finished with `result == "success"`; the three non-matching attestation jobs must be `result == "skipped"`.
    - The normative jq skeleton is logical rather than a literal requirement to pass the entire `needs` object through one environment variable. Implementations must project `needs` down to the compact set of fields the gate actually consumes before handing JSON to `jq`, so runner environment-size limits cannot silently become a correctness bug in larger monorepos.

    Illustrative fragment only; this block is a workflow logic sketch, not standalone valid YAML.

    ```text
        - id: collect-gate-input
            name: Collect compact gate input
            uses: ./.github/actions/collect-gate-input
            with:
                    jobs-json: ${{ toJson(needs) }}
                    include-jobs: resolve-context,static-analysis,build-csharp,build-python,build-jsts,build-ruby,attest-csharp,attest-python,attest-jsts,attest-ruby,require-provenance,create-release-tag,confirm-publish-state,publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher,publish-nuget-official-api-key,publish-npm-official,publish-pypi-official,publish-rubygems-official-trusted-publisher,publish-rubygems-official-api-key,publish-github-official
    - name: Assert official release completeness
      env:
          GATE_INPUT_JSON: ${{ steps.collect-gate-input.outputs.gate-input-json }}
      run: |
          jq -n -e '
              (env.GATE_INPUT_JSON | fromjson) as $n
              | {
                  publishJobs: {
                      "npm:official": "publish-npm-official",
                      "pypi:official": "publish-pypi-official",
                      "github:official": "publish-github-official"
                  },
                  nugetJobs: [
                      "publish-nuget-official-trusted-publisher",
                      "publish-nuget-official-api-key"
                  ],
                  rubygemsJobs: [
                      "publish-rubygems-official-trusted-publisher",
                      "publish-rubygems-official-api-key"
                  ],
                  buildJobs: {
                      "csharp": "build-csharp",
                      "python": "build-python",
                      "jsts": "build-jsts",
                      "ruby": "build-ruby"
                  },
                  attestJobs: {
                      "csharp": "attest-csharp",
                      "python": "attest-python",
                      "jsts": "attest-jsts",
                      "ruby": "attest-ruby"
                  }
              } as $map
              | ($n["resolve-context"].result == "success")
              and ($n["static-analysis"].result == "success")
              and ($n["require-provenance"].result == "success")
              and ($n["create-release-tag"].result == "success")
              and ($n["confirm-publish-state"].result == "success")
              and (($n["create-release-tag"].outputs["tag-result"] == "created") or ($n["create-release-tag"].outputs["tag-result"] == "no-op"))
              and (($n["require-provenance"].outputs["artifact-evidence-url"] | type) == "string")
              and ($n["require-provenance"].outputs["artifact-evidence-url"] != "")
              and (($n["require-provenance"].outputs["release-evidence-head-sha"] | type) == "string")
              and ($n["require-provenance"].outputs["release-evidence-head-sha"] != "")
              and ($n["confirm-publish-state"].outputs["confirmation-state"] == "complete")
              and (($n["confirm-publish-state"].outputs["confirmation-alert"] == "none") or ($n["confirm-publish-state"].outputs["confirmation-alert"] == "serial-degraded"))
              and (
                  ($n["resolve-context"].outputs.targets) as $targets_json
                  | ($targets_json | type) == "string"
                  and ($targets_json != "")
                  and (
                      ($targets_json | fromjson) as $targets
                      | (($targets | index("nuget:official")) != null) as $want_nuget
                      | (($targets | index("rubygems:official")) != null) as $want_rubygems
                      | ([$map.nugetJobs[] | select($n[.].result == "success")]) as $nuget_success_jobs
                      | ([$map.rubygemsJobs[] | select($n[.].result == "success")]) as $rubygems_success_jobs
                      | ($n["confirm-publish-state"].outputs["confirmed-published-targets"] | fromjson) as $confirmed_targets
                      | ($targets
                          | map(
                              if . == "nuget:official"
                              then ($nuget_success_jobs[0] // null)
                              elif . == "rubygems:official"
                              then ($rubygems_success_jobs[0] // null)
                              else $map.publishJobs[.]
                              end
                          )) as $selected_publish_jobs
                      | ($targets | type) == "array"
                      and ($targets | length) > 0
                      and ($confirmed_targets | type) == "array"
                      and ($targets | all(. as $target | if ($target == "nuget:official" or $target == "rubygems:official") then true else $map.publishJobs[$target] != null end))
                      and (if $want_nuget
                          then ($nuget_success_jobs | length) == 1
                               and (($map.nugetJobs - $nuget_success_jobs)
                                  | all(. as $job | $n[$job].result == "skipped"))
                          else ($map.nugetJobs | all(. as $job | $n[$job].result == "skipped"))
                          end)
                      and (if $want_rubygems
                          then ($rubygems_success_jobs | length) == 1
                               and (($map.rubygemsJobs - $rubygems_success_jobs)
                                  | all(. as $job | $n[$job].result == "skipped"))
                          else ($map.rubygemsJobs | all(. as $job | $n[$job].result == "skipped"))
                          end)
                      and ($selected_publish_jobs | all(. != null))
                      and ($selected_publish_jobs | all(. as $job | $n[$job].result == "success"))
                      and ($selected_publish_jobs | all(. as $job | ($n[$job].outputs["publish-result"] == "new-publish" or $n[$job].outputs["publish-result"] == "no-op")))
                      and ($confirmed_targets == $targets)
                      and (if (($targets | index("npm:official")) != null)
                          then (($n["publish-npm-official"].outputs["applied-dist-tags"] | fromjson) == ($n["resolve-context"].outputs["npm-dist-tags"] | fromjson))
                          else true
                          end)
                      and ((([$map.publishJobs[]] + $map.nugetJobs + $map.rubygemsJobs) - $selected_publish_jobs)
                          | all(. as $job | $n[$job].result == "skipped"))
                  )
              )
              and (
                  ($n["resolve-context"].outputs.language) as $lang
                  | ($map.buildJobs[$lang] != null)
                  and ($map.attestJobs[$lang] != null)
                  and ($n[$map.buildJobs[$lang]].result == "success")
                  and ($n[$map.attestJobs[$lang]].result == "success")
                  and (([$map.buildJobs[]] - [$map.buildJobs[$lang]])
                      | all(. as $job | $n[$job].result == "skipped"))
                  and (([$map.attestJobs[]] - [$map.attestJobs[$lang]])
                      | all(. as $job | $n[$job].result == "skipped"))
              )'
    ```
    - The workflow is not complete until this job succeeds. This closes the silent-green path where a publish job is skipped because of wiring drift rather than because the target was absent.

## 5. Release Configuration Contract

Each project that can be released must have a release configuration file at `<project-root>/release.json`. The resolver jobs in `buddy.yml` and `official.yml` read this file to determine publish targets.

**Schema:**

```json
{
    "schemaVersion": 1,
    "targets": ["nuget:gpr", "nuget:official", "github:official"]
}
```

**Fields:**

| Field           | Type       | Required | Description                                                 |
| --------------- | ---------- | -------- | ----------------------------------------------------------- |
| `schemaVersion` | `number`   | Yes      | Release configuration schema version. Current value: `1`.   |
| `targets`       | `string[]` | Yes      | Array of publish targets in `ecosystem:destination` format. |
| `npmAccessHint` | `string`   | No       | Checked-in npm package-access hint for `jsts` projects that declare `npm:*`; closed set `{public, restricted}`. |

**Validation rules:**

- `release.json` must be valid JSON.
- `schemaVersion` must be present and equal to `1`.
- `targets` must be a non-empty array of unique strings.
- Every target must be one of the explicitly supported values in the table below. Unknown values are hard failures.
- Every target must also be compatible with the resolved project language according to the language-target matrix below. Cross-ecosystem target declarations are hard failures.
- `npmAccessHint`, when present, is legal only for `jsts` projects that declare at least one `npm:*` target, must be exactly `public` or `restricted`, and must be rejected for every other language or target set.
- `npmAccessHint = restricted` is invalid for an unscoped npm package name.
- When a project declares `npm:official`, `resolve-context` must hard-fail before build when the checked-in npm package name is scoped and both checked-in `publishConfig.access` plus `npmAccessHint` are absent.
- No fields other than `schemaVersion`, `targets`, and optional `npmAccessHint` are allowed. The validator must enforce this as a strict top-level key whitelist, equivalent to JSON Schema with `additionalProperties: false`.
- A workflow may filter out valid targets that belong to the opposite release channel, but only **after** validation succeeds.
- After channel filtering, the invoking workflow must still have at least one applicable target.
- In this design, Python's unofficial pre-production target is `pypi:testpypi`.
- Removing a previously used target takes effect immediately because backward-compatibility shims are intentionally out of scope before implementation starts. For example, removing `github:official` stops GitHub Release reconciliation on subsequent official runs and leaves any existing GitHub Release on that identity as manual state. The reviewed PR that removes a target must include a target-specific decommission checklist: for `github:official`, enumerate every existing GitHub Release on that identity, decide archival vs deletion, update consumer documentation, and record any follow-up issue; for production package targets, state whether the existing published package remains live, is deprecated, or is withdrawn, and record that decision in the recovery ledger when applicable; for `pypi:testpypi`, delete the corresponding `buddy-testpypi-<project-name>` environment, remove the provider-side TestPyPI trusted-publisher entry bound to that environment, and remove the trust-bearing `pypi:testpypi` inventory entry so no orphan selector state remains. Subsequent official runs should emit a non-blocking warning when such legacy state still exists.
- Unsupported future schema versions are hard failures with operator guidance. Because implementation has not started, schema upgrades are coordinated changes rather than backward-compatible migrations.
- RubyGems versions use the repository's explicit subset policy: `MAJOR.MINOR.PATCH[.suffix...]`, no leading `v`, no `-` or `+`, suffix segments limited to `[0-9A-Za-z]+`, and every suffix segment must independently contain at least one letter. Numeric-only suffix chains such as `1.2.3.1` are rejected, and mixed chains such as `1.2.3.1.rc1` are also rejected because the segment `1` is digit-only.

**Project resolution contract:**

- `project-name` must identify exactly one releasable project in the repository, must be `1..100` characters long, must match `[a-z0-9][a-z0-9._-]*`, and must reject any occurrence of `..`, any trailing `.`, and any `.lock` suffix for ref safety.
- Releasable project identities are canonical ASCII-lowercase names. Repository policy must hard-fail if any releasable project root basename is not already in that canonical lowercase form.
- Releasable `project-name` values must be unique under ASCII lowercase normalization across the repository so workflow concurrency keys cannot alias distinct projects.
- Repository policy must include a CI validation that scans all candidate project roots and hard-fails if two candidate roots collide under ASCII lowercase normalization. For this validation, a candidate project root is any directory whose basename is exactly the candidate `project-name` and whose contents resolve to exactly one workflow language in `{csharp, python, jsts, ruby}`, regardless of whether its `release.json` is missing or invalid.
- Repository policy must also include a CI validation that scans releasable project roots and hard-fails if any such root resolves to more than one workflow language, enforcing the single-language project scope before any release workflow is invoked.
- Project resolution is performed from the repository root by exact leaf-directory-name match: a candidate project root is a directory whose basename is exactly the canonical lowercase `project-name`.
- Language detection is manifest-driven, not file-extension-driven.
